#### (c) `c ? owns(*p) : reads(*p)` (item 7)
Callee `cr(c, p, a0, a1)`: `requires (c != 0) ==> OWNS(p, a0)`, `requires !(c != 0) ==> READS(p, a1)` (two ghost amounts), `ensures` the same atoms, `res == p.v_int`, `p.v_int == old(p.v_int)`; return checks `perm(p.v_int) >= (g_o ? write : none)`, `perm(p.d_int) >= (g_r ? a1 : none)`, `perm(lv) >= (g_o ? a0 : none) + (g_r ? a1 : none)` (the sum counts the exclusive pair once). `cr__wf` asserts `!(g_o && g_r)`. Callers pass `/3` amounts (k atoms + 1), assert the callee's own pair separation `!((c != 0) && !(c != 0))` first, write the cell after the call and exhale it.
| target | what | result |
|---|---|---|
| `c1_ok` | `call_true` (c = 1), `call_false` (c = 0), `call_any(k)`; write after the call; `res == 3` | **verified** (permission returns for both guards) |
| `c1b_chain_ensures` | the read in the `ensures` written as the chain `(g_o ? p.v_int : (g_r ? p.v_int : 0))` | verified (the plain read after two guarded atoms in `c1_ok` verifies too, no chain needed there) |
| `c2_vac` | `assert false` at the end of both callers | exactly two errors, both at the `assert false` (the paths are reachable) |
| `c3_wrong_value` | `ensures res == 4` | exactly two `Postcondition ... res == 4` errors (callers) |
| `c4_overlap_wf` | `c \|\| owns` + unconditional `reads` | exactly **one** error: `Assert might fail. Assertion !(!(c != 0) && true)` in `ov__wf` (c4_overlap_wf.vpr@76); the method `ov` itself verifies |
| `c4b_overlap_vacuous` | the same contract with `requires c == 0` and body `assert false` | only the `__wf` error: **the overlapping contract is vacuous** (inhaled owns + reads exceeds write), so the wf assert is the only thing that finds it |
| `c5_overlap_call` | a caller of `ov` with `assert !(!(k != 0) && true)` (0037 item 8's pair separation) | two errors: the `__wf` assert and the call-site assert (@88) |
| `c6_write_under_not_c` | the callee writes `*p` on both paths | exactly one error: `Assertion !(perm(p.v_int) != write \|\| perm(p.d_int) != write)` (the body's `permission` check, @52) |
| `c7_write_under_c` | the write only under `c != 0` | verified |

#### (d) a function measure over memory (item 8)
`down(p, a)`: `requires` WF, `OWNS(p, a)`, `p.v_int >= 0`; `ensures OWNS(p, a)`, `p.v_int == 0`, `res == 0`; `decreases p.v_int` (plain, no `old`); body `if (*p > 0) { *p -= 1; return tick() + down(p); }` so that a call (`tick`) precedes the recursive one in emission. The explicit check is printed **after the call's permission checks** and before `t0 := tick()`: `assert !(!((p.v_int < old(p.v_int)) && (old(p.v_int) >= 0)))` (callee's measure in the current heap, caller's under `old`).
| target | what | result |
|---|---|---|
| `d1_ok` | as above, `down__wf` asserts `(NN(p) && hv_0_pre >= 0) ==> (p == p)` | **verified** |
| `d1_vac` | `assert false` after the call | exactly one error at it |
| `d2_nodecrease` | the body writes `*p - 0` | exactly one error, **the explicit assert** (d2_nodecrease.vpr@79); Silicon's own check at the call then passes (its condition is assumed) |
| `d2b_nodecrease_no_explicit` | the same without the explicit assert | one error, Silicon's `Method might not terminate. Termination measure might not decrease` at the call (@80): the backstop |
| `d3_wf_live_only` | `down__wf` with no atom framing (the case of a contract that only has `live(p)`): framing = `false` | exactly one error, the `__wf` assert `... ==> false` (@112) |
| `d5_no_tick_ok`, `d5b_no_tick_nodecrease` | no earlier call, no explicit check | verified; one Silicon termination error at the call |
| `d4_chain_ok` | `decreases (p == null ? 0 : (!(p == null) ? p.v_int : 0))`, `requires !(p == null) ==> OWNS`, recursive call under `p != null` | verified |
| `d4_chain_vac`, `d4_chain_nodecrease` | `assert false`; `*p - 0` | one error each (at `assert false`; Silicon's termination error at the call) |

**NOTEs.** (1) `old(p.v_int)` inside a method body's `assert` is accepted and means the entry heap (used by the explicit check); in the method's `decreases` it must stay plain (S28 P6). (2) The measure read needs `hv_m` only in the `__wf` method; the ghost `hv_m_pre` of `down__wf` is a free integer there (the framing assert does not use it). (3) A method whose `requires` holds only the liveness amount and whose measure reads `*p` is silent in Silicon (P6d) and fails only at the `__wf` assert, as item 8 says. (4) Amounts at a call with two exclusive atoms on one argument: `/3` (the generic k + 1) works; nothing needs the exclusivity at the call except the separation assert.

No contradiction of item 7 or 8.

#### Additions after audit round 1 (note 6) and owner question 72
- **`d6_failed_permission_then_measure`** (hand-written, `s29/il/`): `downq(p, q, a)` owns `p` (measure `p.v_int`) and calls itself on `q`, which it does not own, after the explicit permission asserts of `call_atoms`. Silicon reports exactly four errors: the failed asserts `q != null` (@49), `offset_of(q) < len(block_of(q))` (@51), `perm(q.v_int) == write` (@52), and `Method might not terminate. Termination measure might not decrease or might not be bounded` at the call (@59) (the measures of `q` and `p` are unrelated, so this one is legitimate). **There is no `insufficient permission to access q.v_int` error from Silicon evaluating the plain method measure at the call**: the failed asserts are assumed, and the later parts of the check (`perm(q.d_int) == write`, ...) do not fail again. So a call whose explicit permission check failed adds only a `termination`-category report at the call, never an unmapped Silicon error (no exit 3).
- **Partners by path** (owner question 72): the bad trusted contract `int tr(int c, int *p) requires(c ? owns(*p) : reads(*p)) ensures(r, owns(*p));` fails exactly at the `f__wf` assert (`build/m4.5b1c2/lower/cond4.c`, `error: permission: the contract of tr returns *p on a path where its requires did not take it`, line 7), in both modes, from the real driver (not hand-written).

## M4.5b1c3: pointers to pointers, owning parameters, `*result`, written atoms (record 0040)

Probe P62 (the IL and the compiler matrix of `*pp` shapes; il-analyst) and spike S30 (Silicon; il-analyst) of the M4.5b1c3
session, branch `m4.5b1c3-pointers-to-pointers` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/m4.2b1`); evidence under `build/m4.5b1c3/`
(not committed): `p62/`, `s30/`. Silicon 1.1-SNAPSHOT `6b540aa4`, Z3 4.16.0 from `build/env.sh`; Apple clang 21.0.0,
Homebrew GCC 16.2.0. Record 0040 item 2 takes P62's hazards H1 and H2 (conversions that add qualifiers below the first
level) and A8 (the static half of sequencing extended to nested dereferences).

### P62: the IL facts record 0040 relies on (pointers to pointers, `*result`, written atoms) **PASS for A1-A4, A6, A7 as IL facts; two HAZARDS (H1, H2) for item 2's conversion rule, one NOTE per remaining question**

Evidence under `build/m4.5b1c3/p62/` (not committed): inputs `a1.c` (A1), `a2.c` (A2), `a3.c` (A3), `a4.c` (A4), `a5.c`, `a5x.cpp` (A5), `a6.c`, `a6cpp.cpp` (A6), `a7.c` (A7), `a8/S1..S7.c` (A8, `a8/matrix.txt`, raw compiler output `a8/S*.<compiler>.<tier>.txt`). For each input `<f>.c23.il` / `<f>.c++20.il` (`scripts/cerastes-fe.sh --c23|--c++20 --il_display --display_error_number -I include`), `.walk` (`--cerastes_walk`), `.err` (EDG diagnostics); `run.sh <input>` produces them; scratch tools `ilsum.py`, `ilvars.py`, `rawnode.py` (copies of P60/P57's). Branch `m4.5b1c3-pointers-to-pointers`, nothing built, no source touched; `build/cerastes-fe` and `build/cerastes` as they were. C inputs run under `--c++20` as well as `--c23`. `il_def.h` lines are `third_party/edg/src/il_def.h`. Tree notation as in P60 (`L` = `is_lvalue`, `g` = `compiler_generated`, `@n` the column). Apple clang 21.0.0, Homebrew GCC 16.2.0 (`gcc-16`, `g++-16`).

#### Hazards (read first)

- **H1. In C++, EDG accepts `int **` to `const int **` (and the same as a call argument) with only a discretionary warning, where clang and g++ reject it; the driver's `--diag_error` list is C-only.** `a5x.cpp:2` `const int **a = pp;` with `--c++20`: `warning #144-D: a value of type "int **" cannot be used to initialize an entity of type "const int **"` (exit 0, IL produced); `a5.c:17` the same, and `a5.c:23` `g2(pp);` (`void g2(const int **q)`): `warning #167-D: argument of type "int **" is incompatible with parameter of type "const int **"`. The other bad conversions of `a5x.cpp` are real errors in C++: line 3 (drop const, `int *const *` to `int **`), 4 (`long **` to `int **`) and 5 (`const int **` to `int **`) are `error #144`. Native: `clang++ -std=c++20`: `error: cannot initialize a variable of type 'const int **' with an lvalue of type 'int **'` (`a5x.cpp:2`), `g++-16`: `error: invalid conversion from 'int**' to 'const int**' [-fpermissive]`. `src/driver/verify_main.cpp:357` has `if (c_mode) edg.push_back("--diag_error=42,144,167,513");`, so in C++ mode the hole reaches the encoder as a compiler-generated pointer cast (A5). **Control:** `scripts/cerastes-fe.sh --c++20 ... --diag_error=144,167 a5.c` makes exactly `a5.c:17` and `a5.c:23` errors (`error #144-D`, `error #167-D`, "2 errors detected") and leaves `a5.c:9`, `:13`, `:22` (the legal qualification conversions) accepted. The classic unsoundness (`const int **c = pp; *c = &constant; **pp = 1;`) needs exactly this conversion, and record 0040 item 2 says only "C's implicit `int**` to `const int**` stays an incompatible-pointer error" (C only). Either `144,167` join the C++ list too (the rest of #144/#167 is already an error in C++) or the encoder rejects the cast by its types.
- **H2. In C, `int **` to `const int *const *` is accepted with NO EDG diagnostic, while GCC 16 rejects it and clang warns; so the plan's "C's `int**` to `const int**` stays an error" does not cover it.** `a5.c:13` `const int *const *cpp = pp;`, `a5.c:22` `g3(pp);` (`void g3(const int *const *q)`) and `a5.c:28` `if (cq == pp) {}` (`cq` a `const int *const *`): `a5.c23.err` has no #144/#167/#42 for them (only line 17 `#144-D` and line 23 `#167-D`). Native C: `clang -std=c23`: `warning: initializing 'const int *const *' with an expression of type 'int **' discards qualifiers in nested pointer types [-Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers]` (`a5.c:13`; also `:22`) and `warning: comparison of distinct pointer types ... [-Wcompare-distinct-pointer-types]` (`:28`); `gcc-16 -std=c23`: `error: initialization of 'const int * const*' from incompatible pointer type 'int **' [-Wincompatible-pointer-types]` (`:13`, and `:22` "passing argument 1 of 'g3' from incompatible pointer type"), `warning: comparison of distinct pointer types lacks a cast [-Wcompare-distinct-pointer-types]` (`:28`). The IL of these conversions is the same compiler-generated cast as C++'s legal one (A5), so the encoder cannot tell a legal C++ qualification conversion from this C case by the node; only the mode tells. By 0028 item 1 ("every pointer conversion counts"; "strictest when the compilers disagree") the C mode should reject it, in the encoder.

#### A1. `int *p = &x; int **pp = &p; **pp = 5; int z = **pp;`, `*pp = &y`, `*pp = NULL` **PASS, both modes**

Probe `a1.c` (`a1`, lines 2-11). `address_taken` (il_def.h:11389), `python3 ilvars.py a1.c23.il a1` (C++20 identical):
```
variable x  address_taken=TRUE   variable y  address_taken=TRUE   variable p  address_taken=TRUE  type=int *
variable pp address_taken=-      type=int **                      variable z  address_taken=-
```
So `address_taken` is set on the pointer local `p` (by `&p` at `a1.c:6`) and not on `pp`; it is set by the `&` as for an integer (P51 item 2). Node shapes (`python3 ilsum.py a1.c23.il a1`; `++` marks the C++20 difference):
```
a1.c:7  **pp = 5    assign(indirect(indirect(var pp{int **}){int *}){int:L@3}, const[int 5]{int}){int}     C++20: the assign has {int:L}
a1.c:8  z = **pp    init z: indirect(indirect(var pp{int **:@13}){int *:@12}){int:@11}                      (both modes)
a1.c:9  *pp = &y    assign(indirect(var pp{int **}){int *:L@3}, address_of(var y{int:L@10}){int *}){int *}
a1.c:10 *pp = NULL  assign(indirect(var pp{int **}){int *:L@3}, const[int 0]{int *:@9}){int *}              (C++20 the same; the constant's expr is cast(const[?]{long}){int *:g})
```
- **Nesting:** `**pp` is `eok_indirect` of `eok_indirect` of `eok_variable` (il_def.h:13873). The raw nodes of `a1.c:7` (`python3 rawnode.py a1.c23.il a1 eok_indirect 354`): the **inner** `*pp` has `type: int *`, `orig_lvalue_type: int *` and **no** `is_lvalue`; the **outer** has `type: int`, `is_lvalue: TRUE` and no `orig_lvalue_type` line; `var pp` has `orig_lvalue_type: int **`. On the read (`a1.c:8`, `rawnode.py ... eok_indirect 355`) all three nodes have `orig_lvalue_type` and none has `is_lvalue`. So only the outermost node of a store target is the lvalue; the intermediate loads are rvalues (`orig_lvalue_type` marks them as glvalue-derived, il_def.h:14917, :14942), exactly P51 item 1 applied twice. In `*pp = &y` / `*pp = NULL` the target `*pp` is the lvalue of type `int *`.
- The null stored through `pp` is the folded `const[int 0]{int *}` (P51 item 4, P57 (e)).
- `a1.c:14-15` (`a2` in the probe file): `**pp = 1` with `pp = &p`, `p` a parameter: same shape, `p` `address_taken=TRUE param=TRUE`.

#### A2. `&p` of a pointer PARAMETER **PASS, both modes; nothing new beyond 0037 item 4 / P58 (c)**

Probes `a1.c:13-16` and `a2.c` (`a2b`, `a2c`, `a2d`). `ilvars.py a2.c23.il a2d`: `variable p address_taken=TRUE storage=sc_auto param=TRUE used=TRUE type=int *`, `variable r ... param=TRUE address_taken=-` (a parameter whose address is not taken stays `-`), `pp address_taken=-`. One variable per parameter, no copy (P58 (a)); the `init pp: address_of(var p{int *:L@15}){int **:@14}` is the same node as for `&a` of an `int` parameter. Variants (`a2.c`, both modes):
```
a2b  int *const p, &p     variable p address_taken=TRUE type=int *const        init pc: address_of(var p{int *const:L@21}){int *const *:@20}
a2c  int **q, &q          variable q address_taken=TRUE type=int **            init qq: address_of(var q{int **:L@16}){int ***:@15}
```
So a `const`-qualified pointer parameter keeps `int *const` as the variable's type and `&p` is `int *const *` (qualifiers stay in the node types; the field name rule ignores them). `*pp = r; **pp = 1;` (`a2d`, `a2.c:11-12`): `assign(indirect(var pp){int *:L}, var r{int *})` and the `**pp` store as in A1.

#### A3. VeriFast's `address_of_local`, exactly, and `uintptr_t**` **PASS, both modes**

Probe `a3.c` (the two functions at lines 19-33 and 35-49, `inc`/`inc_uintptr_t` with the contracts of `tests/memory/verifast/address_of_local.c`). `ilvars.py a3.c23.il address_of_local` (C++20 identical):
```
variable x address_taken=TRUE type=int   variable ptr address_taken=TRUE type=int *   variable ptrptr address_taken=-  type=int **   variable z address_taken=-
```
```
a3.c:25  init ptrptr: address_of(var ptr{int *:L@23}){int **:@22}
a3.c:26  inc(*ptrptr)  call(routine inc{void (*)(int *)}, indirect(var ptrptr{int **:@12}){int *:@11}){void:@10}      (C++20 the same)
```
**The argument node is a bare `eok_indirect` of `var ptrptr`**, an rvalue (no `is_lvalue`, no `eok_lvalue_adjust`, no `eok_cast`), of type `int *`. The `uintptr_t` function has the same trees with `uintptr_t` types: `variable ptrptr type=uintptr_t **`, `init ptrptr: address_of(var ptr{uintptr_t *:L@29}){uintptr_t **:@28}`, `call(inc_uintptr_t, indirect(var ptrptr{uintptr_t **:@22}){uintptr_t *:@21})`; `init x: const[int 0UL]` (C23, C++20) with the constant's expr `cast(const[int 0]{int}){uintptr_t:g}`. **The typedef chain** (`a3.c23.il`, type `76a20590c0`): `kind: tk_pointer` (il_def.h:5593) with `type_pointed_to` a second `tk_pointer` (`uintptr_t *`), whose pointee is `kind: tk_typeref` (il_def.h:5599, the `type` field at :10739-10745) named `uintptr_t` (`source_corresp name: "uintptr_t"`, `decl_position.seq: 3822`), `typeref_type: unsigned long` (one step on this host; `<stdint.h>` of the macOS SDK has `typedef unsigned long uintptr_t;`). So the field name is computed by skipping typerefs at the leaf and recursing through `tk_pointer`: `v_ptr_ptr_ulong` for the `ptrptr` cell's pointee `uintptr_t *` (the cell `ptr` is `v_ptr_ulong`, `x` is `v_ulong`). The printed type string keeps the typedef (`uintptr_t **`), so any name derived from the printed string would differ; derive it from the type nodes. The `assert` macro expands to `__builtin_expect`/`__assert_rtn` (`a3.c23.il` `L4869`), unchanged from `address_of_local.c`'s existing functions.

#### A4. `int ***ppp` (depth 3) **PASS, both modes**

Probe `a4.c` (`a4`). `ilvars.py a4.c23.il a4`: `x`, `p`, `pp` `address_taken=TRUE`, `ppp` `-`, `z` `-` (each pointer variable whose address is taken, at every level). Trees (C++20 differs only by the assign's `{...:L}`):
```

a4.c:7  z = ***ppp   init z: indirect(indirect(indirect(var ppp{int ***:@14}){int **:@13}){int *:@12}){int:@11}

a5.c:13  const int *const *cpp = pp;          init cpp: cast(var pp{int **:@27}){const int *const *:g@27}

Which of them EDG diagnoses (`.err` files; `--display_error_number`):

| Shape | C23 | C++20 |
|---|---|---|

| `int *const *` to `int **`; `long **` to `int **`; `const int **` to `int **` (`a5x.cpp:3-5`) | not run in C | `error #144` |
| `cq == pp` (`:28`, distinct pointer types) | accepted, none (no #42) | accepted, none |

`int *const *` and `const int **` as parameter types (`g1`, `g2`) print as such in the IL (`g1{void (*)(int *const *)}`). Native C compilers on the same file: see H2 (clang warns at the default tier, GCC 16 errors); native C++: both reject only `a5.c:17`/`:23`.

#### A6. `*result` in an `ensures`, both spellings **PASS: `*r` reaches the IL as `eok_indirect` of the binder, an rvalue**

Probes `a6.c` (macros `CERASTES_ENSURES(r, ...)`, run in both modes, `a6.c23.walk`, `a6.c++20.walk`) and `a6cpp.cpp` (`[[cerastes::ensures(r, ...)]]` written out, `a6cpp.c++20.walk`; after removing the `pp_result` function its normalised walk is identical to `a6.c++20.walk`). `*r == 1` (`a6.c:17`, `pick`), `walk` excerpt, C23:
```
attr [[cerastes::ensures]] on routine @ L17:5
  arg 1 binder r: int * @ L17:22
  arg 2 @ L17:25
    op eok_land ... op eok_eq @ L17:27 ( binder r: int * @ L17:25 , param 1 p: int * @ L17:30 )          r == p
    op eok_eq type_kind=tk_integer type=int @ L17:50 ( op eok_indirect type_kind=tk_pointer type=int @ L17:47 ( binder r: int * @ L17:48 ) , const 1 type=int @ L17:53 )     *r == 1
```
C++20 the same with `type=bool`. **The `*r` indirect is an rvalue in both modes (no `lvalue` in the walker line; a contract's `owns(*p)` argument is printed `lvalue`)**, and its operand is a bare `binder r` (the same node as the result in `r == p`; arg 1 of the attribute declares it). `pp_result` (`int **` result, `a6.c:34-39`): `op eok_indirect type=int * ( binder r: int ** )` against `old(*q)`.
- **`cerastes_old(*r)` (C, `a6.c:30` `pick_old_r`, `*p == OLD(*r)`)** survives the front end intact, in the same shape as `old(*p)` of a parameter (`a6.c23.walk:84-90`): `op eok_indirect type=int ( op eok_cast type=int * cast=c-style ( op eok_call type=const void * routine cerastes_old_ ( op eok_cast type=const void * cast=implicit ( binder r: int * ))))`; the `&(*r)` inside the macro is folded to the bare binder. C++ (`cerastes::old(*r)`, `a6.c++20.walk:91-99`): `op eok_ref_indirect type=int ( op eok_call type=const int & routine cerastes::old args <T=int> ( op eok_reference_to ( op eok_lvalue_adjust type=const int lvalue ( op eok_indirect type=int lvalue ( binder r: int * )))))`. So `old(*r)` reaches the encoder and can be rejected there by the binder under the indirect; today `build/cerastes verify a6.c --std=c23`: `error #cerastes-unsupported_expression: "cerastes::old" applied to the result is not supported` (`a6.c:30`), and `a6.c:17`/`:24` give `a dereference of the result in an `ensures` (M4.5b1c3: ...)`. `old(*r)` with `r` a `T**` result is the same shape one level up.

#### A7. Written atoms in `CERASTES_INVARIANT`; `owns(*pp)` / `owns(**pp)` in contracts **PASS: no new node kinds beyond P59**

Probe `a7.c` (`l1`..`l6`, `c1`..`c5`), `a7.c23.walk`, `a7.c++20.walk`. **Variables:** in a loop annotation a pointer local and a (reassigned or not) parameter are both `var q: int * decl=L<n>:<c>` (P59 item 1 NOTE; `l2`, a reassigned parameter: `a7.c23.walk` `var q: int * decl=L22:14`), not `param 1 q`; they are told apart by `is_parameter` only. Shapes (C23; C++20 differences stated):
- **`OWNS(*q) && i >= 0`** (`l1`, `a7.c:19`): `eok_land( eok_call cerastes_owns( eok_indirect(var q) ), eok_ge ...)`. C++20: `eok_call cerastes::owns args <T=int> ( eok_reference_to ( eok_lvalue_adjust ( eok_indirect lvalue (var q))))`.
- **`q == NULL || OWNS(*q)`** (`l2`, `:24`): `eok_lor( eok_eq(var q, const 0 type=int *), eok_call cerastes_owns(...))`; C++20 the same with `bool` types.
- **`c ? OWNS(*q) : READS(*q)`** (`l3`, `:30`): C23: `eok_question ( var c , eok_cast type=int cast=implicit ( eok_call cerastes_owns ) , eok_cast type=int cast=implicit ( eok_call cerastes_reads ) )`: **the arms are `eok_cast` to `int` of the `_Bool` calls, and the condition is the bare `var c`**; C++20: `eok_question type=bool ( eok_bool_cast ( var c ) , eok_call cerastes::owns , eok_call cerastes::reads )` (no casts on the arms, `bool_cast` on the condition). The two arms are separate call nodes over two separate `var q` nodes.
- **`LIVE(q) && READS(*q)`** (`l4`, `:36`) and **`OWNS(*q) && READS(*s) && LIVE(q)`** (`l5`, `:45`): as P59 item 1 (`cerastes_live` of the bare `var q`; C++20 `cerastes::live` over `eok_cast ... cast=implicit` of `var q`).
- **`OWNS(*q) && *q == 0`** (`l6`, `:51`): the read `eok_eq( eok_indirect(var q), const 0)`, the indirect an rvalue (no flag), beside the atom.
- **NOTE (warnings):** EDG warns for a pointer only written or named in annotations: `a7.c:22` `warning #550-D: parameter "q" was set but never used` (`l2`), `:42` `variable "q"`, `:43` `variable "s"` (`l5`), both modes, as in P59. A test of `q` read only in its invariant carries these (or is made to use `q` in the body).
- **`owns(*pp)` / `owns(**pp)` in a contract** (`c1`..`c5`, `a7.c:55-72`): the **nesting of `eok_indirect` is the whole difference.** C23 `OWNS(*pp)` (`c1`): `eok_call cerastes_owns ( eok_indirect type=int * ( param 1 pp: int ** ) )`; `OWNS(**pp)` (`c2`): `eok_call cerastes_owns ( eok_indirect type=int ( eok_indirect type=int * ( param 1 pp: int ** ) ) )`. C++20 `owns(*pp)` is `cerastes::owns args <T=int *>: bool (*)(int *const &)` over `eok_reference_to type=int *const & ( eok_lvalue_adjust type=int *const lvalue ( eok_indirect type=int * lvalue ( param 1 pp ) ) )`; `owns(**pp)` is `args <T=int>: ... (const int &)` over `eok_lvalue_adjust ( eok_indirect type=int lvalue ( eok_indirect type=int * ( param 1 pp ) ) )` (`a7.c++20.walk:160-171`). **So the encoder tells `*param` from `**param` by the depth of `eok_indirect` over `param` (the inner one is an rvalue, the outer carries `lvalue` in C++), and in C++ also by the template argument `T` (`int *` against `int`).** `c3` (`OWNS(*pp) && *pp != NULL && READS(**pp)`) shows the read `*pp` as a bare rvalue `eok_indirect type=int *` under `eok_ne(..., const 0 type=int *)`, and `c4` `LIVE(*pp)`: C23 `cerastes_live( eok_indirect type=int * (param 1 pp))`, C++20 `cerastes::live args <T=int> ( eok_cast type=const int * cast=implicit ( eok_indirect type=int * (param 1 pp)))`.

#### A8. Sequencing keys: `-Wunsequenced` / `-Wsequence-point` on pointer-to-pointer shapes **PASS: results below; nothing new beyond P61's "clang names objects syntactically"**

Seven shapes (`a8/S1.c`..`S7.c`, `int x = 0, y = 0, r = 0; int *p = &x; int **pp = &p;` and `r = (int)(<shape>);`), tiers D (no flag), A (`-Wall`), E (`-Wall -Wextra`), `-fsyntax-only`, Apple clang 21 and GCC 16.2, `-std=c23` / `-std=c++20`; `a8/matrix.txt`:

| Shape | clang C, C++ (D, A, E) | gcc C | gcc C++ |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 `(*pp = &y, **pp)` | silent | silent | silent |
| S2 `**pp + (*pp = &y, 0)` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E (`S2.c:6:25: operation on '* pp' may be undefined`) |
| S3 `**pp + (**pp = 1)` | silent | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E (`operation on '**pp'`) |
| S4 `(*pp == (*pp = &y))` | silent | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | same |
| S5 `**pp + (p = &y, 0)` (aliasing by name) | silent | silent | silent |
| S6 `(**pp = (*pp = &y, 5))` | silent | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | same |
| S7 `(*pp = &y) == *pp` | silent | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | same |

Never at the no-flag tier D, in any compiler or mode; **clang never warns on any `pp` shape** (its check names objects syntactically, P61); GCC warns at `-Wall` on the shapes that name `*pp` or `**pp` twice (S3, S4, S6, S7, and S2 only in g++), and on none that reach the same cell by another name (S5) or are sequenced by a comma (S1). EDG itself warns on none of them (`a8` run under `--c23`/`--c++20`: no sequence diagnostic, only #550-D for `y`). By the union rule of 0039 item 3 (a warning at no flag or `-Wall` in some compiler and mode): S2, S3, S4, S6, S7 are rejected as `unsequenced_modification` shapes (`*pp` and `**pp` are objects named twice, like `*p`), S1 and S5 are accepted and left to the path-precise `unsequenced` category. `build/cerastes verify a8/S2.c` today stops earlier at `int **pp`: `error #cerastes-unsupported_type: type "int ** (a pointer to a pointer: M4.5b1c3)" is not supported`.

#### Other notes

- **NOTE (`address_taken` on the pointer, not the pointee chain):** `address_taken` is set on exactly the variable whose `&` is written (`a4.c`: `x`, `p`, `pp` TRUE, `ppp` `-`); the plan's rule "a pointer variable whose address is taken is a cell" is directly readable from the flag, with no contradiction to record 0040 items 2-6.
- **NOTE (loads are rvalues, no lvalue-to-rvalue node):** P51 item 1 holds at every level: `*pp` read as a pointer is an `eok_indirect` without `is_lvalue` (A1), so the encoder's value/place split for `*pp` is the same as for `*p`.

### S30: Silicon on pointer cells, `*result` and written atoms (record 0040 items 2, 4, 5) **PASS for (a), (b), (c); five findings the record lacks (F1-F5), none an unsound frame**

Evidence under `build/m4.5b1c3/s30/` (not committed): `gen_a.py`, `gen_a2.py`, `gen_a3.py`, `gen_b.py`, `gen_c.py`, `gen_c1.py`..`gen_c3.py` (generators; `prelude.py` has the shared pieces, taken from the real emitted Viper of `emitted/*.vpr`: `cell_across_loop`, `loop_owns_fill`, `live_result`, `swap_owns`, `loop_pointer_write`, `cell_conditional_target`), `targets/*.vpr` with `<t>.out` (Silicon output, exit, wall seconds, load average before) and `.time`; `sv.sh` (copy of S29's) runs the pinned Silicon 1.1-SNAPSHOT `6b540aa4` with Z3 4.16.0. Re-run: `bash build/m4.5b1c3/s30/sv.sh build/m4.5b1c3/s30/targets/<name>.vpr`. Every run was made alone, with `--numberOfErrorsToReport 0` (all errors listed); the machine was loaded (one-minute averages 77-150, the figures in the tables are upper bounds). The hand-written targets follow the emitted shapes of the tests above, with the record's additions (`v_ptr_int`/`d_ptr_int` fields, `alloc_ptr_int`, `WF` for the range, the amounts and checks of item 5). Each OK target has a twin that fails at the one intended assertion (the "first error" below is the first one Silicon lists, in program order); the vacuity controls `c2_vac_tie`, `c3_vac_tied` (`assert false` at the end of the loop body) fail, so the OK targets are not vacuous.

#### (a) Pointer cells (item 2)

| Target | Shape | Result | Silicon time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a1_address_of_local` | VeriFast's `address_of_local`: `x` and `ptr` cells, `ptrptr := ptr`, `inc(*ptrptr)` (call checks on the loaded pointer, amount `perm(lv)/2`), `z == 1`, scope exits | verifies | 5.7 s |
| `a1_twin_wrong_value` | `z == 2` | `Assert might fail ... v_z == 2` | 6.0 s |
| `a1_twin_dangling` | `*p` read after the block of `&y` ended: the loaded pointer's own liveness check | `Assertion t != null ==> perm(lvloc(block_of(t)).lv) > none` (the first and only error) | 6.1 s |
| `a1_twin_null` | `*pp = NULL; **pp = 5` | `Assertion t != null` | 6.2 s |
| `a2_loop_ptr_cell` | a loop writing `*pp = &y` over automatic places `x`, `y` (int cells) and `p` (the pointer cell), the `WF` row, the user's `p == x \|\| p == y`, then `**pp` | verifies | 7.4 s |
| `a2_twin_havoc_no_invariant` | no invariant about the cell's value | first error `t != null ==> perm(lvloc(block_of(t)).lv) > none` (the lifetime error of the havoc), then `t != null`, `perm(t.v_int) > none` | 10.4 s |
| `a2_wf_row_present` / `a2_twin_wf_row_dropped` | after the loop `assert WF(t)` with no user invariant | verifies / `Assertion t == null \|\| t == loc(...) ...` fails | 9.6 s / 11.0 s |
| `a3_set_ok` | `set(pp, q)`: `requires owns(*pp) && live(q)`, `ensures owns(*pp) && live(q) && *pp == q` (the callee verified with a body; a caller reads `*pp == y` and `**pp`) | verifies | 9.1 s |
| `a3_twin_callee_stores_null` / `a3_twin_weak_callee_contract` / `a3_twin_caller_without_cell` | callee stores null / ensures without `*pp == q` / the caller's cell already released | `p_pp.v_ptr_int == p_q` / `t == v_y` / `perm(v_ptrptr.v_ptr_int) == write` (each the only error) | 8.3 s / 8.0 s / 6.0 s |

- **F1 (a case split the record lacks): a pointer loaded from a cell needs the same case splits as a call's pointer result (0037 item 3).** After the loop of `a2_loop_ptr_cell` the value of `*pp` is only known to be `x` or `y`; the load `t := pp.v_ptr_int` followed by `t.d_int` fails with `insufficient permission to access t.d_int` unless `if (v_ptr.v_ptr_int == v_x) { }`, `if (... == v_y) { }` (against every automatic place of the loaded pointer's pointee field, and the liveness cells likewise) come first (`a2_twin_no_case_split`: one error at the `t.d_int` read; with the splits it verifies). The same splits belong at the load of a pointer wherever its value is not a known Ref (after a loop, after a call that stores into the cell). Item 2 must say it, next to item 4's callers' splits (`result_splits`, `lower.cpp` :3431).
- **F2 (the `WF` row is needed and sufficient):** without `kv > none && kd > none && d_ptr_int ==> WF(v_ptr_int)` the loaded pointer after a loop is not `WF` (`a2_twin_wf_row_dropped`); with it `WF(t)` holds with no user invariant (`a2_wf_row_present`).
- The loaded pointer's liveness check is Silicon-visible: `a1_twin_dangling` fails there and nowhere earlier; the liveness of a stored pointer (`assert v != null ==> perm(lvloc(block_of(v)).lv) > none` before the store) held in every OK target.
- **F3 (the loop's places include every cell whose address the body stores or whose liveness a store checks).** In the first draft of `a2_loop_ptr_cell` only the pointer cell was in the invariant: the store `*pp = &y` inside the body then failed its liveness check on `y` (`perm(lvloc(block_of(v_y)).lv) > none`), because a Viper loop body sees only what the invariant holds. So `x` and `y` must be automatic places of that loop (they are, by 0038 item 3: every cell with permission in scope). Item 2's "a store ... is a use (liveness)" is covered by 0038 item 3 and needs no new rule, but the loop-place set must contain a cell the loop only *names* through `&y`; check that `loop_places` collects them.

#### (b) `*result` (item 4)

| Target | Shape | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b1_pick_ok` | `int *pick(int *p)`: `requires owns(*p)`, `ensures(r, r == p && owns(*p) && *r == old(*p))`: the read `res.v_int` is plain (`res == p` is an earlier conjunct of the same `ensures`, so the guard implies the framing disjunct); the `f__wf` method has the result-keyed ghost `hv_r_post`, the prior fact `res == p_p ==> hv_r_post == hv_0_post` and no framing assert; a caller reads `*q` after `q := pick(&x)` with the split `if (v_q == v_x) { }` and gets the value | verifies | 6.4 s |

Unframed, the chain in the *method's* `ensures` is `D ? res.v_int : 0`, which a caller reads as `false` on the `!D` path (a vacuous contract), so the `f__wf` assert is what keeps it sound: `b3` shows it fails alone. Item 4 should say the method itself verifies and only `f__wf` reports.

#### (c) Written atoms (item 5)

Setting (all targets): a Viper loop whose invariant holds, in this order, the counter's bounds, the automatic rows of every place the loop holds (cells `x`, `y` and, where a parameter is not reassigned, the parameter's place, with their snapshots `kl kv kd vs ds` and the guards `gv`/`gl` of `lower.cpp` :4018 for a place equal to an earlier one), then each written atom's rows (`atom_rows` in `gen_c.py`: `q != null && WF(q) && bound`; `NOTAUTO ==> acc(q.v_int, a_v) && acc(q.d_int, a_d) && q.d_int && range`; `q == x_i ==> kv_i == write && kd_i == write` (`reads`: `> none`); `AND_i lvloc(q) != L_i ==> acc(lv, a_l)`; `q == x_i ==> kl_i > none`), with ghost `Perm` amounts assigned before the loop; the case splits of item 5 before the snapshots and at the top of the body; the explicit asserts at entry and after the body (the back edge).

- **F5 (separation is a spec-meaning check, not a soundness one, for automatic places):** two `owns` atoms on `q` and `s` that name the same *automatic* place verify without the explicit separation assert (`c6_twin_no_explicit_check`): both atoms' automatic rows just say `kv == write` of one place. So the explicit `q != s` assert is the only thing that rejects `owns(*q) && owns(*s)` with `q == s`, and it must be emitted at entry and at the back edge for every pair with an `owns` among atoms of one field, automatic or not; for two non-automatic places Silicon's own exhale also fails, so there the assert only reorders the error.
- **A second-order requirement (F6):** a loop over several parameter places needs, besides item 5's splits, the method-entry split `if (lvloc(block_of(p_p)) == lvloc(block_of(p_s))) { }` and the `gv`/`gl` guards on the second place's `acc` rows, or Silicon fails `Loop invariant acc(lvloc(block_of(p_s)).lv, kl_ps)` on entry in the shared-cell branch (my first draft of `c6_control_distinct`). The existing `lower.cpp` (:3960-3983, :4018-4072) already has both for atoms of parameters; the written atoms must pass through it (their `q`s are not parameters, so their splits are item 5's).
- **Order of reporting:** every failing explicit assert is one `assert` statement; Silicon continues after a failed assert, so a missing permission at entry gives a *list* of errors in program order (`c8`: `v_p != null`, `offset_of(v_p) < len(...)`, `perm == write`). The first is the atom's, in source terms; the encoder reports one error per annotation position, as for calls.
- No spike contradicted record 0040 items 2, 4 or 5 in substance; F1 and F3 are additions to item 2 (the loaded pointer's splits; the loop's places), F4 a clarification of item 4, F5 and F6 of item 5.

### P63: the IL facts record 0041 relies on (mutable globals, `static` locals, `&g`, `g` in contracts, `main`) **PASS for A1-A8 as IL facts; no outright CONTRADICTION of items 2-11; eight HAZARDS (H1-H8) the reader and the lowering must handle, six NOTEs**

Evidence under `build/m4.5b2a/p63/` (not committed). Probe inputs `a1.c`, `a1b.c`, `a1n.cpp`, `a1c.cpp` (A1), `a2.c`, `a2b.c`, `a2c.cpp`, `a2d.c` (A2), `a3.c`, `a3x.cpp` (A3), `a4.c`, `a4b.c`, `a4c.c` (A4), `a5.c`, `a5x.cpp` (A5), `a6.c`, `a6b.c`, `a6x.cpp` (A6), `a7.c`, `a7n.cpp`, `a7b.cpp`, `a7c.cpp` (A7), `a8/` (A8), `a9.c`, `a9b.c` (A9). For each input `<f>.c23.il` / `<f>.c++20.il` (`scripts/cerastes-fe.sh --c23|--c++20 --il_display --display_error_number -I include`), `.walk` (`--cerastes_walk`), `.err`; `run.sh <input>` produces them (a `.cpp` runs C++20 only; **a `.c` runs both modes, so a `.c` and a `.cpp` with the same base name overwrite each other's `.c++20.*`; that is why `a1n.cpp`, `a3x.cpp`, `a7n.cpp` exist**). Scratch readers: `gvars.py` (file-scope variable fields), `cons.py` (one line per initializer constant), `etree.py` (the expression trees of a function with raw node kinds, constants' `expr:` shown as `<orig expr: ...>`), `slocals.py` (static locals and their init entries), `routines.py`, plus P62's `ilsum.py`, `ilvars.py`, `rawnode.py`, `sttree.py`. Branch `m4.5b2a-globals`, nothing built or touched in the tree (`build/cerastes-fe` as it was). Both modes for every C probe. `il_def.h` lines are `third_party/edg/src/il_def.h`. Notation: `{T L g @c}` = type, `is_lvalue`, `compiler_generated`, column. `seq` of a position is a running source-sequence number (it equals the line only in a file with no includes; `a1.c` has none, `a2.c` includes `<stddef.h>` and shows seq 352...), so evidence below cites the probe line.

#### Hazards (read first)

- **H1. `&g` has two node shapes, and the shape depends on the context and the mode; in C++ some comparisons of addresses are folded to an integer.** `a4.c` (C23, `etree.py a4.c23.il <fn>`; C++20 the same unless stated):
  ```
  a4.c:10 return &g;            eok_address_of(enk_variable g {int L}) {int *}                       (bare)
  a4.c:11 return *&g;           eok_indirect(eok_address_of(enk_variable g {int L}) {int *}) {int}    (bare; not folded to g)
  a4.c:20 *&g = 9;              eok_assign(eok_indirect(eok_address_of(enk_variable g)), const 9)     (bare)
  a4.c:15 return &g + 1;        eok_padd(eok_address_of(enk_variable g) {int *}, enk_constant ck_integer 1) {int *}   (bare)
  a4.c:12 p = &g;               eok_assign(enk_variable p, enk_constant ck_address address.kind=abk_variable variable=g off=0 <orig expr: eok_address_of(enk_variable g {int L})> {int *})
  a4.c:13 callee(&g);           eok_call(routine callee, enk_constant ck_address ... variable=g off=0 <orig expr: eok_address_of(...)> {int *})
  a4.c:14 &g == p               eok_eq(enk_constant ck_address ... variable=g off=0 <orig expr: eok_address_of(...)>, enk_variable p)        (C++: wrapped in eok_cast to int)
  a4.c:16 &g != &h              C23: eok_ne(enk_constant ck_address g, enk_constant ck_address h)      C++20: enk_constant ck_integer integer_value=1 <orig expr: eok_cast(enk_constant ck_integer 1 <orig expr: eok_ne(ck_address g, ck_address h)>)>
  a4.c:19 (c ? &g : &h) == gp   C23: eok_question(var c, enk_constant ck_address g, enk_constant ck_address h)     C++20: eok_question(eok_bool_cast(var c), eok_address_of(var g), eok_address_of(var h))   (bare arms)
  ```
  So `&g` is `eok_address_of` over `enk_variable` (return value, `*`/`+` operand, assignment target), or an `enk_constant` of `ck_address`/`abk_variable` (assignment source, call argument, comparison operand, conditional arm in C; the constant's `expr:` keeps the original `eok_address_of` tree), and C++ differs from C in the conditional's arms. `&g != &h` is `ck_integer 1` in C++ and `&g == &g` / `&g == 0` are `ck_integer` 1 / 0 in both modes (`a4b.c:5` `e2`, `:8` `e5`, with the folded tree in `expr:`). `&g + 1` as a comparison operand or call argument is `enk_constant ck_address ... off=4` (`a4b.c:4` `e1`, `:7` `e4`; `<orig expr: eok_padd(eok_address_of(var g), const 1)>`). `&*&g` is a constant `ck_address g off=0` in both modes (C `<orig>` is `eok_address_of(var g)`, C++ keeps `eok_address_of(eok_indirect(eok_address_of(var g)))`, `a4b.c:9`). **The encoder must accept both shapes everywhere an address is read (`address_of`, `constant`), and treat a folded integer comparison as a value it must still accept (0024's reader).**
- **H2. An `enk_constant ck_address` is not always `&g` written: in C, a later read of a const pointer local initialized with `&g` is folded to the same constant, with `<orig expr: enk_variable p>`.** `a4b.c:15` `void e12(void) { int *const p = &g; (void)p; }`: C23 `eok_cast(enk_constant ck_address address.kind=abk_variable variable=g off=0  <orig expr: enk_variable p {int * @43}> {int * @43}) {void}`; C++20 `eok_cast(enk_variable p {int *const @43})`. The constant's `expr:` tells them apart (`eok_address_of` against `enk_variable`).
- **H3. An explicit pointer cast of `&h` is a `ck_address` with the same `variable` and `offset` as `&h` and only the constant's `type` changed: the reader must compare the constant's pointee type with the variable's type, in initializers and in code.** `a2d.c:2-4`: `char *cp = (char *)&h0;` is `kind: ck_address`, `address.kind: abk_variable`, `variable: h0`, `address.offset: 0`, `type: char *`, constant text `(char *)(&h0)` (`cons.py a2d.c23.il`, C++20 identical); likewise `long *`, `void *`, `unsigned int *`, and `long **` over `&q` (`a2d.c:9`, `pql`). No diagnostic from EDG in either mode. In code, `a4c.c:2` `(char *)&g == p`: `eok_eq(enk_constant ck_address ... variable=g off=0 <orig expr: eok_cast(enk_constant ck_address ... <orig: eok_address_of(var g)> {int *}) {char *}> {char * @26}, var p)`. `const` is stripped the same way: `a2.c:22` `int *gp7 = (int *)&k;` (`const int k`) is `ck_address`, `variable: k`, `type: int *`, `orig_type: const int *`, so "the address of a const object" must be tested on the target variable's own type, not the constant's.
- **H4. A null pointer initializer is a `ck_integer` of value 0 whose `type` is the pointer type; the existing `ck_integer`-only reader (`encode.cpp:1721`) would read it as an integer.** `cons.py a2.c23.il`: `gp3 | int * | initk_static | (int *)0 | ck_integer`, `gp4 (NULL)` the same text `(int *)0` with `explicit_cast_applied: TRUE` (C's `((void*)0)`); `a2b.c:3` C23 `nullptr` is `(int *)nullptr` `ck_integer` value 0; C++20 `NULL` is `(int *)__null` `ck_integer` value 0 with `null_keyword: TRUE`, **`is_simple_zero` absent** (`a2.c++20`, `gp4`), while `0` and `(int *)0` have `is_simple_zero: TRUE`; a function pointer null is the same (`fp`, `(int (*)(void))0`). So a null is: `kind == ck_integer`, `type` a pointer, `integer_value` 0. `is_simple_zero` is not the test.
- **H5. `&h - 0` and `&h + 0` keep `ck_address` with offset 0 but a non-NULL `subobject_path`; `&h + 1` is offset 4 (bytes) with `subobject_path` `is_offset`, `ptr_offset: 1`.** `a2.c:28` `int *gp10 = &h1 - 0;` (constant text `&h1`): `address.offset: 0`, `subobject_path: file-scope subobject-path` with `ptr_offset: 0`; `a2.c:20` `gp6 = &h0 + 1`: `address.offset: 4`, `ptr_offset: 1` (il_def.h:5219 `subobject_path`, :5216 `offset` in bytes, :4647 `ptr_offset`). `one_past_the_end` (il_def.h:5144) is not printed for it. The reader should reject on `address.offset != 0` (a `subobject_path != NULL` with `ptr_offset == 0` is the same address as `&h`).
- **H6. A static local's initializer is not on the variable when `init_kind == initk_function_local`; it is in a `local-static-variable-init` entry on the scope's `local_static_variable_inits`.** `slocals.py a6b.c23.il` (C++20 the same, `a6b.c++20.il`, and `a6x.cpp`): `f::count = 0` and `f4::c4 = 1`, `f3::c3 = 5` are `initk_static` with the constant on the variable; `f3::p = &c3` (`a6.c:3`), `f5::c5 = 2 + 3` (`:5`), `f11::b` (`static unsigned char b = 1`) and `bb` (`static _Bool bb = 1`) are `initk_function_local` and the entry says `init_kind=initk_static constant=&c3 ck=ck_address ... variable=c3 off=0`, `constant=5 ck=ck_integer`, `constant=(unsigned char)1U`, `constant=(bool)1U`; the C++ dynamic `static int s = ext();` (`a6x.cpp:2`) is `init_kind=initk_dynamic` with `dynamic ... dik=dik_expression` (il_def.h:11074 `a_local_static_variable_init`, :18548 the scope list, :11747-11754 `init_kind` and the empty variant). A `static int c = 0` or `1` (literal of the variable's own type) stays on the variable (`initk_static`).
- **H7. A C++ `constexpr` call in a global's initializer is folded: `initk_static`, a `ck_integer`, and the `expr:` of the constant is the `eok_call` tree.** `a3x.cpp:5` `int g3 = cf();` (`constexpr int cf()`): `init_kind: initk_static`, constant `4`, `expr` node `operation.kind: eok_call`, `operation.type_kind: tk_unknown`; `a3x.cpp:4` `sizeof(int)` and `:6` `2 * sizeof(long)` are `ck_integer` 4 and 16 under a generated `eok_cast`. 0017's reader (calls rejected in a constant, `const_depth`) would refuse `g3` although the front end has its value (the value is correct; the encoder must choose to read the value or refuse).
- **H8. A `dik_constant` initializer of an automatic `int *q = &g` / `&v`, which 0032 never met for locals.** `a4.c:12` `int *p = &g;`: `variable p init_kind=initk_dynamic ... dynamic-init p kind=dik_constant` with the `ck_address` constant (`a6b.c:9`, `int *q = &v` with `v` a static local: `dynamic-init ... kind: dik_constant`, `constant: &v`, `ck_address`, `abk_variable`, `variable: v`, `address.offset: 0`, `subobject_path: NULL`). For `&x` of an automatic `x` the initializer is `dik_expression`; the local-initializer reader meets `dik_constant` only now.

Facts the encoder reads:
- **Linkage:** `source_corresp.name_linkage == nlk_internal` for `static`, an unnamed namespace, and a C++ `const` (which is also `storage_class sc_static`); otherwise external. External is `nlk_external` in C but **`nlk_cplusplus_external` in C++, except that `extern "C" int ec = 1;` in C++ has `name_linkage C`** (`a1n.cpp:9`), so question 84's "external in C++" must be decided by `il_header.source_language`, not by `name_linkage == nlk_external`.
- **Storage class:** `storage_class` is the effective one (`sc_static` for an unnamed-namespace variable and a C++ `const`, `sc_unspecified` for `extern int h7 = 7;`, whose written `extern` is only in `declared_storage_class`).
- **Defined in this unit:** `declared_type != NULL` (il_def.h:11814: "NULL if there is no defining declaration"; the three extern-only declarations have `declared_type: NULL` and every defined one has a type). Equivalent in all probes: `!(storage_class == sc_extern && init_kind == initk_none)`. The current 0017 test `init_kind == initk_none && storage_class == sc_extern` (`encode.cpp:1749`) is right for all of these.
- **A tentative definition and a C++ default-initialized definition have the same IL** (`initk_none`, `declared_type` set, `sc_unspecified`/`sc_static`) in both languages; both are zero-initialized (static storage). `initk_zero` was never produced for a scalar (`int br = {0}; int be = {};`, `int br{};` are `initk_static` constant 0; il_def.h:11021 says it "also serves to distinguish a tentative definition", but not in this configuration).
- **One variable entity per object:** two tentative definitions, `extern` then a definition (also a block-scope `extern int late;` before the file-scope definition, `a9b.c:1-2`: `cons.py a9b.c23.il late` gives the one variable `initk_static 4`, position 2:5), tentative then initialized: a single `a_variable`; its `decl_position` is the first tentative definition or **the defining declaration** (`g5` 7:5, `t` 5:5, `u` 7:5), not the first appearance. The other declarations are `src-seq-secondary-decl` entries (the same type as routines' secondary declarations in `il_query.cpp:94`, which today collects only routines).
- **Unreferenced globals are kept:** `a9.c:1` `int unused = 5;` `needed: TRUE`; `a9.c:2` `static int us = 1;` `referenced: FALSE`, `needed: FALSE`, still a variable of the file scope with `init_kind initk_static`.
- **`const` against mutable** (what `is_const_object`, `encode.cpp:1627`, reads: `f_get_type_qualifiers(v->type, TRUE) & TQ_CONST` or `v->is_constexpr`): `a1b.c:8` `const int k` type `const int` (`tk_typeref` over `int`); `:9` `int *const cp = 0` type `int *const`, a **const object** (kind `tk_typeref` with `qualifiers: const`, il_def.h:6249 `a_type_qualifier`), mutable `const int *pc` (`:10`) type `const int *` is a `tk_pointer` whose pointee is const: **mutable**; `static const int sk` (`:11`) `sc_static`, const. The `volatile int gv` type prints `volatile int`, `_Atomic int ga` prints `_Atomic(int)`, `_Thread_local int tl` has `is_thread_local: TRUE` (`a9.c:3-5`, C23); `int arr[3]` `int [3]`, `struct S gs` `struct S`, `void *vp` `void *` all `initk_none` (`a9.c:6-8`).
- **Position:** `source_corresp.decl_position` (`seq`, `column`) is the identifier's position; for `g1` it is `1:5` (the column of `g1`), not of the specifier.

`ck_ptr_to_member` did not occur (no pointer to member was written). **Fields to read:** `v->init_kind`, `v->initializer.constant` (`constant->kind`, `constant->type`, `constant->variant.address.kind`, `.variant.address.variant.variable`, `.offset`, `.subobject_path`), **and `constant->type` against the variable's type** (H3, H4). #### A3. C++ initializers that are not constants **PASS**

Probe `a3x.cpp` (C++20), `cons.py a3x.c++20.il`:
- `a3x.cpp:3` `int g1 = f();`: `init_kind: initk_dynamic`, `dynamic: file-scope dynamic-init`, whose `kind: dik_expression` and `expression:` the call (il_def.h:3962 `a_dynamic_init_kind`, :11052 the union's `dynamic`); no `constant:`. `a3x.cpp:8` `int g5 = h;` (h a mutable global) and `:9` `int *g6 = new int(3);` are `initk_dynamic` too (`g5`, `g6`).
- `a3x.cpp:4` `int g2 = sizeof(int);` is `initk_static`, `ck_integer` 4, `expr:` a generated `eok_cast` over the constant (`type_kind: tk_integer`); `:6` `2 * sizeof(long)` is 16; `:10` `(int)sizeof(char) + 1` is 2. **`:5` `int g3 = cf();` (a `constexpr` function) is `initk_static` with the folded value 4 (H7).**
- C23: `a3.c:2` `int g1 = f();` is `error #59: function call is not allowed in a constant expression`, and `a3.c:5` `int g5 = h;` is `error #28: expression must have a constant value`; no IL, so in C a dynamic initializer cannot reach the encoder.

#### A4. Uses in code **PASS; see H1, H2, H8**

Probe `a4.c`, `a4b.c`, `etree.py`. A read `g` is `enk_variable g` with `orig_lvalue_type: int` (`a4.c:5`) and no `is_lvalue` (an rvalue, not folded to the initial value, as P51 says for locals); a write target and `g++`/`++g` operand are `enk_variable g {int L}` (`a4.c:6` `eok_assign(enk_variable g {int L}, const 1)`, `:7` `eok_post_incr(enk_variable g {int L})`, `:8` `eok_pre_incr`, `:9` `eok_add_assign`); **C++20 differs only in the `{...:L}` flag of the assign/compound-assign result and the `bool` wrapper of comparisons, as in P51/P62**. `*gp` (a pointer global read) is `eok_indirect(enk_variable gp orig_lvalue_type=int *)` (`a4.c:17`); `gp = &h; *gp = 7;` (`:18`) is `eok_assign(enk_variable gp {int * L}, enk_constant ck_address ... variable=h ...)` and `eok_assign(eok_indirect(enk_variable gp) {int L}, const 7)`. `&g` forms: H1. `callee(&g)` is the constant (`:13`). `address_taken` is `TRUE` on `g` in every probe that writes `&g` in code (`a4.c`), **and not reliable otherwise** (A5, A9 note).

#### A5. Uses in contracts **PASS: everything reaches the IL; `old(g)` differs by mode**

Probes `a5.c` (C spellings, run in both modes) and `a5x.cpp` (`cerastes::`), `--cerastes_walk` (`a5.c23.walk`, `a5.c++20.walk`, `a5x.c++20.walk`). A global in a contract is `var g: int decl=L2:5` (the walker prints the declaration position; there is no `param`/`binder`), an `enk_variable` whose variable has `enclosing_routine NULL`.
- **C `cerastes_owns(g)` / `cerastes_reads(g)` (`a5.c:5`, `:6`):** `op eok_call type=bool ( routine cerastes_owns: bool (*)(...) , var g: int decl=L2:5 )`; **the argument is the bare `var g`, an rvalue, unlike `owns(*p)` whose argument is `op eok_indirect`**. In C++ mode the same C spelling prints the same.
- **C++ `cerastes::owns(g)` (`a5x.cpp:5`):** `routine cerastes::owns args <T=int>: bool (*)(const int &) noexcept` over `op eok_reference_to type=const int & ( op eok_lvalue_adjust type=const int lvalue ( var g: int decl=L2:5 lvalue ) )`; `cerastes::reads` the same; a pointer global `cerastes::owns(gp)` has `<T=int *>` and `int *const &` over `eok_lvalue_adjust type=int *const lvalue ( var gp lvalue )` (`a5x.cpp:17`).
- **`old(g)`, C (`a5.c:9`, `cerastes_old(g)` = `(*(__typeof__(g)*)cerastes_old_(&(g)))`):** `op eok_indirect type=int ( op eok_cast type=int * cast=c-style ( op eok_call type=const void * routine cerastes_old_ ( const (const void *)(&g) type=const void * )))`: **the `&g` is an `enk_constant`, `ck_address`, `address.kind abk_variable`, `variable: g`, `address.offset: 0`, `subobject_path: NULL`, type `const void *`** (`a5.c23.il` `constant@7b6e076820`, with `expr:` the cast tree) in both modes. For a parameter `old(*p)` has no such constant (P62 A6).
- **`old(g)`, C++ (`a5x.cpp:9`):** `op eok_ref_indirect type=int ( op eok_call type=const int & routine cerastes::old args <T=int> ( op eok_reference_to ( op eok_lvalue_adjust type=const int lvalue ( var g lvalue ))))`: the plain variable under `lvalue_adjust`, no address constant.
- **`g > 0`, `g == ...`, `g < 100`** (`a5.c:8`, `:11`): `op eok_gt ( var g , const 0 )`, plain `var g` rvalue operands; **`CERASTES_DECREASES(g)` (`a5.c:15`, `a5x.cpp:14`): `attr [[cerastes::decreases]] arg 1 var g: int decl=L2:5 lvalue`** (the only form of `g` carrying `lvalue` in C).
- **`CERASTES_INVARIANT(g >= 0)` (`a5.c:21`):** `stmt stmk_while @ L22 attr [[cerastes::invariant]] arg 1 op eok_ge ( var g , const 0 )`, both modes (same shape as P59 for locals).
- **`cerastes_owns(gp) && cerastes_owns(*gp)` (`a5.c:25`):** `op eok_call cerastes_owns ( var gp: int * decl=L4:6 )` and `op eok_call cerastes_owns ( op eok_indirect type=int ( var gp ) )` (C++ `T=int *` and `T=int`, `eok_indirect type=int lvalue ( var gp )`), the P62 A7 shape with a global base.
- **`cerastes_live(&g)` (C spelling, `a5.c:28`):** `op eok_address_of type=int * ( var g lvalue )` (both modes). C++ `cerastes::live(&g)` (`a5x.cpp:20`) prints `const (const int *)(&g) type=const int *`, the address constant (H1's second shape under a conversion). `cerastes::live(g)` is `error #304` (`live` takes a pointer).
- **`cerastes_owns(*&g)`** (`a5.c:29`): `eok_indirect ( eok_address_of ( var g lvalue ) )`.
- **NOTE (`address_taken` and contracts):** `a5.c23.il`/`a5.c++20.il` have **no** `address_taken` on `g` (although `&(g)` and `&g` appear in `old(g)` and `live(&g)`), `h` `TRUE` (from `gp = &h`); `a5x.c++20.il` has `address_taken: TRUE` on `g` and `gp` (reference binding and `live(&g)`). So `address_taken` is not a reliable flag for a global: it does not need to be, since every global and static local is a block.

#### A6. `static` locals **PASS: readable; the initializer sits in a scope list (H6)**

Probes `a6.c` (C23), `a6b.c` (both modes; `a6.c` has `_Bool`, an error in C++20), `a6x.cpp`; `python3 slocals.py <dump>`; `python3 sttree.py`. Facts, **identical in C23 and C++20 for the shared shapes** (`diff` of `slocals.py a6b.c23.il` and `a6b.c++20.il` is empty; the trees differ only in `{bool}` against `{int}` of conditions):
- **Telling it apart from an automatic:** `source_corresp.enclosing_routine` is the routine (`file-scope routine: f`), `is_local_to_function: TRUE`, `parent_via_local_scope_ref: TRUE` (so `parent_scope` is NULL, il_def.h:3407), **`name_linkage: no`**, **`storage_class: sc_static`** (an automatic is `sc_auto`: `etree.py` prints `storage_class=sc_auto` for `n`, `q`, `x`). Its position is its own declaration (`f::count 1:26`, `f3::p 3:48`), not the function's. It is a variable in the routine's `scope-orphaned-list-header` (`orphaned_variables: ... count`, il_def.h:16978), and a `stmk_decl` in the body's statement list (`sttree.py a6b.c23.il f3`: two `stmk_decl` for `c3` and `p`), with no `stmk_init` (an automatic's initializer `int x = ca;` has a `stmk_init`, `f6`).
- **Initializer** (H6): `a6.c:1` `static int count = 0;` `init_kind: initk_static`, constant 0, `is_simple_zero`; `a6.c:2` `static int c2;` `initk_none` (zero, static storage); `a6.c:3` `static int *p = &c3;` `initk_function_local`, entry `constant=&c3 ck=ck_address ... variable=c3 off=0`; `a6.c:5` `static int c5 = 2 + 3;` `initk_function_local`, entry `constant=5`; `a6.c:7` `static const int k = 9;` `initk_static`, and **a use of `k` is folded to `enk_constant ck_integer integer_value=9 <orig expr: enk_variable k>`** (`etree.py a6.c23.il f7`); `a6x.cpp:2` `static int s = ext();` `initk_function_local`, entry `init_kind=initk_dynamic`, `dik_expression`; `a6x.cpp:9` `static int *np = nullptr;` entry `constant=(int *)nullptr ck_integer`.
- **`thread_local`:** `a6.c:11` `static _Thread_local int t` and `a6x.cpp:4` `static thread_local int t`: `is_thread_local: TRUE`, `storage_class: sc_static`, `init_kind: initk_static`.
- **Recursion:** `a6.c:4` `f4(int n)` with `static int c4 = 1;` and the recursive call: `c4` is one variable (`initk_static`), `etree.py` shows `eok_call(routine f4 ...)` between its reads and the write; nothing in the IL ties the call to the static.
- **Address flag:** `address_taken: TRUE` on a static local whose `&` is written (`f3::c3` through the `static int *p = &c3` entry, `f9::v` through `int *q = &v`), `-` otherwise; meaningful for code, not needed (every static local is a block).
- **Several statics in one function, same name:** `a6.c:8` `f8` has two variables named `u1` in nested blocks (`slocals.py`: two `f8::u1` lines, positions 8:27 and 8:48); EDG warns `#177-D variable "u1" was declared but never referenced` for the outer. `GB_<name>__<id>` needs the id, as the plan has.

`is_main` reads `source_corresp.name == "main"` and `!source_corresp.is_class_member` only, so it is true for `ns::main` (the `--cerastes_walk` lists it as `routine ns::main plain body @ L1:20`, `a7n.c++20.walk`). **The global-namespace `main` is the routine with `name == "main"`, `is_class_member` false and `source_corresp.parent_scope->kind == sck_file`** (il_def.h:18214, :3302; `ns::main` is `sck_namespace`, `S::main` is a class member); `type` is `int (void)` in C and `int ()` in C++ for the no-parameter form, `int (int, char **)` for the other.

#### A8. Compiler matrix of same-object unsequenced shapes on a global **PASS: results below (rule of 0039 item 3: a warning at no flag or `-Wall` in some compiler and mode)**

`a8/gen.py` writes `a8/src/<id>.{ext,stat}.{c,cpp}` (one shape in `int fn(...)` with `r = (int)(<shape>);`, `g` external or `static`, `int *gp = &g;`, `p` a parameter where the shape uses it, `int bump(void) { g += 1; return g; }`), runs Apple clang 21.0.0 (`clang`/`clang++` of `/usr/bin`; `xcrun --find clang` is the Command Line Tools'), Homebrew GCC 16.2.0 (`gcc-16`, `g++-16`), `-std=c23`/`-std=c++20`, tiers D (none), A (`-Wall`), E (`-Wall -Wextra`), `-fsyntax-only` and for GCC also `-O2 -c -o /dev/null` at D (`a8/results.json`, `a8/matrix.md`, `a8/raw/<id>.<link>.<compiler>.<tier>.<syntax|O2>.txt`, 504 runs). No run produced an error; external and `static` `g` give identical cells for every shape.

| Shape | clang C | clang C++ | gcc C | g++ C++ | Verdict (union) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 `g++ + g`, G3 `g + g++`, G4 `(g = 1) + g` | `-Wunsequenced` at D, A, E | `-Wunsequenced` at D, A, E | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | `-Wsequence-point` at A, E | **reject** |
| G2 `g = g++`, G11 `g = (g = 1)` | `-Wunsequenced` at D | **silent** | `-Wsequence-point` A, E | `-Wsequence-point` A, E | **reject** (as P61's A2: clang C++ silent, g++ warns) |
| G12 `g += g++` | `-Wunsequenced` at D | silent | `-Wsequence-point` A, E | **silent** | **reject** (clang C, gcc C) |
| G5 `*&g + g++`, G18 `(*&g = 1) + g` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` A, E | **silent** | **reject** (gcc C only: GCC resolves `*&g` to `g` in C, not in C++) |
| G6 `g++ + *p`, G7 `*p + g++`, G10 `*p = g++` (p a parameter), G8 `g++ + *gp`, G9 `*gp + g++` (`gp = &g`) | silent | silent | silent | silent | path-precise `unsequenced` only |
| G13 `g + bump()`, G14 `bump() + g`, G15 `g++ + bump()`, G16 `bump() + bump()`, G17 `g + g` | silent | silent | silent | silent | not rejected as a shape (the call rule of 0020/0039 item 4 applies) |

GCC `-O2 -c` at D: silent for every shape (`-Wsequence-point` is `-Wall` only). Nothing is `-Wextra`-only. Same classification as locals in P61 (A1-A10) for G1-G4, G2, G11; the new fact is G5/G18 (`*&g`, gcc-C only) and that G8/G9 (`*gp`) behave like B shapes (silent), so item 10's "`*&g` read as `g`" rejects the G5/G18 shapes in both modes (by the union), and `g++ + *p`/`*gp` is `unsequenced` path-precisely only.

#### A9. Other surprises (notes)

- **N1. A block-scope `extern int ext_in_block;` is a file-scope `a_variable`** (`enclosing_routine: NULL`, `storage_class: sc_extern`, `declared_type: NULL`, `a9.c:10`), indistinguishable from a file-scope `extern int x;` by the variable; it is a `stmk_decl` in the function (`encode.cpp:3016` rejects it there today). With a definition later in the file it is the same entity as the definition (`a9b.c`).
- **N2. `volatile`, `_Atomic`, `_Thread_local` globals are plain `a_variable` entries** whose type prints `volatile int` / `_Atomic(int)` and `is_thread_local: TRUE` (`a9.c:3-5`); array, struct and `void *` globals have `initk_none` and their types (`a9.c:6-8`); the existing type check (`vtype`) sees them first.
- **N3. A C `static` global that is never referenced is still an `a_variable` of the file scope** (`referenced: FALSE`, `needed: FALSE`, A1); whether `ents.variables` (il_query.h:66, "those not declared inside a routine") lists it was not probed here.
- **N4. C `int g = 0;` and `int g;` differ in IL** only by `init_kind` (`initk_static` with `is_simple_zero` against `initk_none`); both are 0 at start (C 6.7.10p10).
- **N5. `inline int in = 1;` (C++17)** has `is_inline: TRUE` and external linkage (`C++`); it is defined once with that value, like any external C++ global for question 84.
- **N6. Folded `ck_integer` reads of `const` objects:** a use of a `const` global/static local (`static const int k = 9;`, `a6.c:7`) is `enk_constant ck_integer` with `<orig expr: enk_variable k>`, as 0017 item 5 already handles for named constants.

No CONTRADICTION that needs the owner; the following need to be in the record or the code:

## M4.5b2b: initialization through pointers (record 0042)

### P64: P54 re-run on the real registration (record 0042 items 2–8) **PASS; no contradiction of P54; one mode difference (`&*q`)**

Evidence in `build/m4.5b2b/P64/` (not committed): `P64.md` (every claim with its probe line, an excerpt of the output and
the `il_def.h` field), the probes `p01`–`p12`, the runner `run_all.sh` (both modes, every probe), `ildump.py` and the raw
outputs `out/<probe>.<mode>.{il,walk,diags,attrs,calls,vars}`. Registration under test: `{"uninit","","v:+a!"}`,
`{"ref_to_uninit","","p"}`, `{"must_init","","p"}`, all `RAF_NO_FLAGS`; commands `scripts/cerastes-fe.sh --c23|--c++20
--display_error_number --il_display <probe>` and the same with `--cerastes_walk`. Fields: `an_attribute` (il_def.h 3162,
`kind` 3166, `syntactic_location` 3172), `a_param_type.attributes` (6544), `a_source_correspondence.attributes` (3614),
`a_routine_type_supplement.param_type_list` (7401) and `assoc_routine` (7421), `a_variable.init_kind` (11747),
`storage_class` (11254), `address_taken` (11389).

- **A. Parameters (both modes identical).** The markers land on the `param-type` of each declaration that writes them,
  leading (`syntactic_location=prefix`) or trailing (`declarator-id`), on `int **`, beside `owning`, through
  `CERASTES_*` and user macros (`position.seq` the use, `orig_seq` the macro body). Redeclarations accumulate on the
  routine's param-type (no must-match; prototype plus definition, three declarations, different markers on two), and each
  declaration's own function type keeps its own markers, so declarations can be compared one by one. A marker in a
  typedef'd function type reaches the routine declared through it, also when the definition's list has none (A8).
  Registration accepts, for the encoder to reject: both markers, a marker twice, a non-pointer, a `const` pointee,
  `void *`, a variadic function, a marker inside a function-pointer parameter's own list (on the inner function type), a
  C++ reference parameter, members and templates; `int *const p` and a leading marker on `int p[]` are pointer
  parameters. EDG refuses (#1835) an unnamed parameter's marker, a trailing marker on an array parameter and one after a
  function declarator.
- **B. `uninit` on locals (both modes).** On `source_corresp.attributes` of the variable, leading and trailing, on every
  shape (scalar, pointer, `int **`, enum, `bool`, `char`, array, struct, a `for` init). A leading marker over `int a, b
  = 1;` reaches both declarators; `init_kind` tells them apart (`initk_none` without an initializer, `initk_dynamic` for
  `= 1`, `= {}`, `(3)` and C++ `int x{}`). Twice is recorded twice. `--il_display` prints a function-scope variable's
  attribute only as a pointer; the walker shows its name.
- **C. EDG's own refusals (both modes, exit 2):** `uninit` on a global or a `static` local #1862 ("requires an automatic
  variable"); on a parameter, a field or a function #1835; `ref_to_uninit` and `must_init` on a local, a global, a
  function or a field #1835. P54's "`ref_to_uninit` accepted on a local pointer, a global pointer and a function" came
  from its wider prototype registration (targets `p|v|r`); with `p` alone EDG refuses all three, as record 0042 item 2
  expects.
- **D. Call arguments (strict mode, item 8).** `&x` is `eok_address_of` over the variable (the marker is on the variable,
  not in the expression); a parameter passed on and a pointer local holding `&x` are both a bare `enk_variable`, so the
  encoder decides from what the variable is (the VIR argument: the parameter's copy); `NULL`, `0` and `nullptr` are a
  pointer-typed `enk_constant`, `ck_integer`, value 0. **Mode difference:** C23 folds `&*q` to `q` (a parameter passed
  on), C++20 keeps `eok_address_of` over `eok_indirect`, which the encoder rejects in code everywhere since 0032 (record
  0042 item 8). A cast `(int *)&x` is `eok_cast` over the address; `&r[0]` an address of a subscript.

### S32: Silicon on the markers' shapes (record 0042 items 5–7) **PASS for (a)–(f); the vacuity run fails as it must**

Hand-written fixtures, kept: `tests/viper-smoke/memory/s32_{a..f}_*.vpr` (11 files, each with its `// expect:` lines; run

| default member initializer (`DefInit` :12) | supplement `has_field_initializer: TRUE` (:9009), field `has_initializer=TRUE` (:12019); the implicit default constructor is `compiler_generated` but not trivial |
| reference member (`RefM` :13) | `field r : int &` (`tk_pointer`, `is_reference`); the implicit `operator=` is `compiler_generated ... is_deleted=TRUE` |
| virtual (`Virt` :14) | type flag `any_virtual_functions: TRUE` (:10475); routine `f ... is_virtual=TRUE` |
| member template (`TplHolder` :19) | routine `m ... is_template_function=TRUE is_prototype_instantiation=TRUE` |

The class test that `classify.py` applies and that rejects every row above except the first: *every routine in `assoc_scope.routines` is
`compiler_generated` and has `is_trivial_copy_function`, `is_trivial_default_constructor` or `is_trivial_destructor` and is not `is_deleted`
(il_def.h:12458, 12492, 12497, 12502, 12999); no `base_classes`; no virtual; no `has_field_initializer`; no `static` variable in the
scope; every field public.* `c2.cpp:1-10` gives ACCEPT for `Plain`, `Base`, `WithMem` and REJECT for the others, `DT` with a user destructor and `DefA` with a
defaulted `operator=` included.

**The index `k` of a member** is its position in the struct type's `field_list` (`a_type.variant.class_struct_union`), a `next` chain in
declaration order (`a1.c`, `struct S { int x; int y; }`):
```
type@...ee70 struct S   field_list: field@...f3b0: x     field@...f3b0 x: next: field@...f640: y, offset: 0    field@...f640 y: next: NULL, offset: 4
```
A member reached through `enk_field` has `field` pointing at that `a_field`; the containing struct is the field's `source_corresp.parent_scope`, a scope
of `kind: sck_class_struct_union` whose `assoc_type` is the struct (`a1.c`: `parent_scope: file-scope scope@...f1c0`, `assoc_type: ... struct S`), and
equally the type of the first operand of the `dot_field`/`points_to_field`. A nested path `s.t.x` is two `enk_field` selections (item 3); its
index path is `[index of t in S, index of x in T]`. Fields are in declaration order with no gaps (an unnamed bit-field would be an entry; an anonymous member is rejected).

**2. `address_taken`: PASS (both modes identical).** `m1.c` (`ilsum` `VAR` lines; `-` means the flag line is absent, so FALSE):

| Source | Variable | `address_taken` |
|---|---|---|
| `m1.c:3` `s1.x = 1; return s1.x;` | `s1` | absent (FALSE): `s.x` without `&` does not mark `s` |
| `:4` `int *p = &s2.x;` | `s2` | `address_taken=TRUE` |
| `:5` `struct S *p = &s3;` | `s3` | TRUE |
| `:6`, `:10`, `:11`, `:12` `p4->x`, `(*p8).x`, `&p9->x`, `&p10->t` | `p4`, `p8`, `p9`, `p10` (parameters) | absent: `p->x` and `&p->x` never mark `p` |
| `:7` `s5.t.x = 1; return s5.t.x;` | `s5` | absent |
| `:8` `&s6.t`, `:9` `&s7.t.y` | `s6`, `s7` | TRUE (the whole root is marked) |
| `:14` `(&s12)->x` | `s12` | TRUE |
| `:15` `sizeof(&s13.x)` | `s13` | absent (unevaluated, as P57) |
| `sp1.c:8-9` `a = &s; pp = &a;` | `s`, `a` | TRUE for both (`s` by `&s`, the struct pointer `a` by `&a`) |

(`a_variable.address_taken` il_def.h:11389.) So a struct local is only marked by `&` on it or on a path under it; record 0043 item 4 allocates
every struct local as a block regardless, and needs no flag.

**3. Member access: PASS; shapes as P51's table rows, same in both modes.** `m2.c` (`struct S { int x; int y; struct T t; struct S *next; int *q; }`,
`g1(struct S *p, struct S s)`); `eok_dot_field` is declared at il_def.h:14181 (not 14174), `eok_points_to_field` :14185, `enk_field` :13583. Both take
two operands, the second an `enk_field` whose `field` is the `a_field`; the raw nodes of `a1.c:4` `s.x = 1`:
```
expr-node@..c6c0  type: struct S  is_lvalue: TRUE  kind: enk_variable  variable: s
expr-node@..c730  type: int       next: NULL       kind: enk_field     field: x
expr-node@..c7a0  type: int       is_lvalue: TRUE  kind: enk_operation operation.kind: eok_dot_field  operands: ..c6c0   (operation.type_kind: tk_unknown)
```
| Source (`m2.c` line) | Tree |
|---|---|
| `s.x` rvalue (:5) | `dot_field(var s{struct S:L}, field x{int}){int<-same}`: the rvalue has `orig_lvalue_type` and no `L`; no lvalue-to-rvalue node |
| `p->x` (:6) | `points_to_field(var p{struct S *<-same}, field x{int}){int<-same}` |
| `(*p).x` (:7) | `dot_field(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, field x)` |
| `s.t.x` (:8) | `dot_field(dot_field(var s{struct S:L}, field t{struct T}){struct T:L}, field x)` |
| `p->t.x` (:9) | `dot_field(points_to_field(var p, field t{struct T}){struct T:L}, field x)` |
| `(&s)->x` (:10) | `points_to_field(address_of(var s{struct S:L}){struct S *}, field x)` |
| `=` target (:11-15) | `assign(dot_field(var s, field x){int:L}, const[int 1])`, `assign(points_to_field(var p, field x){int:L}, ...)`, `assign(dot_field(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, field y){int:L}, ...)`, `assign(dot_field(dot_field(var s, t){struct T:L}, x){int:L}, ...)`, `assign(dot_field(points_to_field(var p, t){struct T:L}, y){int:L}, ...)` |
| `+=`, `-=`, `++`, `--` (:16-19) | `add_assign(dot_field(...){int:L}, const 6)`, `subtract_assign(points_to_field(...){int:L}, ...)`, `post_incr(dot_field(...){int:L})`, `pre_decr(points_to_field(...){int:L})` |
| `&` (:21-27) | `address_of(dot_field(var s, field x){int:L}){int *}`, `address_of(points_to_field(var p, x){int:L})`, `address_of(points_to_field(var p, field t{struct T}){struct T:L}){struct T *}`, `address_of(dot_field(var s, t){struct T:L})`, `address_of(var s{struct S:L}){struct S *}`, `address_of(dot_field(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, field y))`, `address_of(dot_field(points_to_field(var p, t){struct T:L}, y))` |
| a pointer member (:28-33) | `points_to_field(var p, field next{struct S *}){struct S *<-same}`, `points_to_field(points_to_field(var p, next){struct S *<-same}, field x)`, `assign(indirect(points_to_field(var p, field q{int *}){int *<-same}){int:L}, const 1)`, `indirect(dot_field(var s, field q))`, `assign(points_to_field(var p, field next){struct S *:L}, var p)`, `assign(points_to_field(var p, q){int *:L}, address_of(points_to_field(var p, x){int:L}){int *})` |

The member's own type is the node type (`{int}`, `{struct T}`, `{struct S *}`); there are no casts around a member access. A member read in
arithmetic is converted like a variable (`m3.c:5` `cast(dot_field(var s, field c{char}){char<-same}){int:g}`, `:7` `cast(points_to_field(var p, field e{enum E}){enum E<-same}){unsigned int:g}`
in C and `{int:g}` in C++); members of `char`, `bool`, enum and `unsigned` type assign without a cast on the member (`m3.c:8-11`). The `m2.c` trees differ between the
modes only in the `L` flag of assignment results and in the four implicit `operator=` routines C++ adds (item 5). The `L` flag is set on a member read in a write
position and on the intermediate `{struct T:L}` of `s.t.x` and `p->t.x`; the final read has `orig_lvalue_type`.

**4. Initializers: PASS; every element is kept, in source order.** An automatic struct local is `init_kind: initk_dynamic` with `dynamic: dynamic-init`, plus a
`stmk_decl` followed by a `stmk_init` whose `dynamic_init` is the same node (`i1.c:4-6`); with no initializer, `init_kind: initk_none` and only the `stmk_decl`
(`a1.c:3`, `i3.cpp:29` `S s16;`). The initializer is a `dik_constant` over a `ck_aggregate` (all elements constant), or a `dik_nonconstant_aggregate` over a
`ck_aggregate` whose non-constant elements are `ck_dynamic_init` constants (each holding a `dik_expression`) and whose `has_dynamic_init_component` is TRUE. Aggregate
fields: `first_constant`..`last_constant` chained by `next` (il_def.h:5310-5311), flags `explicit_braces_on_aggregate` :4889, `uses_designated_initializers` :4908,
`is_partially_initialized` :4154 (on the aggregate and on the `dynamic-init`), `is_braced_initializer`; kinds `dik_constant` :3969, `dik_nonconstant_aggregate` :3983,
`ck_aggregate` :3661, `ck_designator` :3667, `ck_dynamic_init` :3656. Trees (`ilsum`, C23 unless marked):

| `{}` (:11) | `aggr{}[struct S explicit_braces_on_aggregate is_partially_initialized]` (C23 and C++20 `i3.cpp:10-11`) |
| `{0}` (:12), `{1}` (:13) | `aggr{const[int 0]{int is_simple_zero}}`, `aggr{const[int 1]}`: **trailing members absent** |
| `{{1, 2}, 3}` (:14) | `aggr{aggr{1, 2}[struct T explicit_braces_on_aggregate], 3}` |
| brace elision `{1, 2, 3}` (:15) | `aggr{aggr{1, 2}[struct T], 3}`: **EDG builds the nested aggregate; the inner one has no `explicit_braces_on_aggregate`**; `i4.c:12` `{1,2,3,4}` for two nested structs likewise; `i4.c:6` `struct N n = {0}` (first member a struct) gives `aggr{aggr{const[int 0]}[struct T is_partially_initialized]}` |

| constant and dynamic mixed (`i2.c:24` `{a + 1, -1}`) | `aggr{dyn(dik_expression: add(var a, const 1)), const[int -1]}` |
| pointer members (:22-23) | `{1, 0}`: `const[int 0]{int * is_simple_zero implicit_cast ...}` (a null pointer constant of pointer type); `{1, &a}`: `dyn(dik_expression: address_of(var a))`; `i6.c:4` `{1, &g}` (a global): `dik_constant ... const[addr abk_variable off=0]{int *}` as an element |

`ck_designator.field` is the `a_field` (il_def.h:5548-5549); il_display prints its name. C++20 (`i3.cpp`): `S s1{1, 2}` and `S s2 = {1, 2}` (:8-9), `{}`, `{0}`, `{1}`
(:10-13), the nested and non-constant forms (:17-23, :31) and `E e1{1, E::K1, true}` (:32) are the same shapes as C; `S s7{.x = 1, .y = 2}` (:14) is
`aggr{desig(.x), 1, desig(.y), 2}`; `S s13(1, 2)` (:26) is `dik_constant: aggr{1, 2}[S]` with no `is_braced_initializer` and no `explicit_braces_on_aggregate`;
`S s14 = S{1, 2}` (:27) `aggr{1, 2}[S explicit_braces_on_aggregate implicit_cast explicit_cast_applied]`; `S s15 = S()` (:28) `aggr{const[int 0], const[int 0]}[S explicit_cast_applied]` (zeros
written out); `S s16;` (:29) `initk_none`. **H1 (mode difference): in C++20 a designated list that skips a member gets an explicit
compiler-generated zero in the skipped place**: `S s8{.y = 2}` (:15) is `aggr{const[int 0]{int}, desig(.y), const[int 2]}`, `i5.cpp:4` `S s3{.y = 1, .x = 2}` is `aggr{0, desig(.y), 1, desig(.x), 2}` and `i5.cpp:5`
`Q q1{.b = 1, 2}` is `aggr{0, desig(.b), 1, 2}`; in C the same lists have no filler (`i2.c:9`). The filler constant has **no `decl_position`** (the written constants and designators have
`decl_position.seq`), and a later designator can name the same field (`x` above), so "a field initialized twice" cannot be told from the list shape alone: the cursor rule (a
designator sets the cursor to its field, every other element takes the cursor field and advances it, the last store to a leaf wins) gives the
right values in all rows above, and a duplicate check must skip the fillers. `i5.cpp:6` `{.a = 1, .a = 2}` in C++ and `i4.c:10` in C have the same duplicate in the IL.

**5. Copies: PASS; trivial C++ copies are plain `eok_assign` or a `dik_expression`.** `c1.c` (C23, `struct S { int x; int y; struct T t; struct S *next; }`, `cp(struct S *p, struct S *q, struct S s)`):
```
:5  t = s            assign(var t{struct S:L}, var s{struct S<-same}){struct S:u}
:6  struct S u = s;  init u: dik_expression: var s{struct S<-same}
:7  *p = *q          assign(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, indirect(var q){struct S<-same}){struct S:u}
:8  *p = s           assign(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, var s{struct S<-same})
:9  s = *p           assign(var s{struct S:L}, indirect(var p){struct S<-same})
:10 p->t = s.t       assign(points_to_field(var p, field t){struct T:L}, dot_field(var s, field t){struct T<-same}){struct T:u}
:11 *p = *p          assign(indirect(var p){struct S:L}, indirect(var p){struct S<-same})
:12 struct S v = *p; init v: dik_expression: indirect(var p){struct S<-same}
:13 (t = s).x        init r: dot_field(assign(var t{struct S:L}, var s){struct S}, field x{int})
:14 struct S w = (t = s);   init w: dik_expression: assign(var t{struct S:L}, var s){struct S}
:15 t = (struct S){1, 2}    assign(var t{struct S:L}, enk_temp_init(){struct S<-same})
```
In C the `assign` result is an rvalue (`{struct S}`, `{struct S:u}` as a statement); in C++ it is an lvalue (`{S:Lu}` as a statement, `{S:L}` as the operand of `.x` at :13, `{S<-same}` as the initializer of `w` at :14); the rest is identical. The struct `assign` has
`operation.type_kind: tk_struct` (`c1.c`, all 9 in both modes) and no call or memcpy: il_def.h:14120 documents it as the bitwise copy ("In lowered C++ IL or in C ... a normal C struct copy"). A compound
literal is `enk_temp_init` (il_def.h:13585), as P51 noted for C.

C++20 (`c2.cpp`, `Plain { int x; int y; }`): **every trivially copyable class is copied by `eok_assign` or by `dik_expression`, never by a call**: `Plain` `:12` `Plain a2 = a;` `init a2: dik_expression: var a`, `:13` `assign(var a2{Plain:L}, var a){Plain:Lu}`,
`:24-27` `Plain a3(a)`, `Plain a4{a}`, `Plain a5 = Plain(a)`, `static_cast<Plain>(a)` are all `dik_expression: var a`. **A non-trivial copy is a call:** `UA` (user `operator=`) `:15` `ref_indirect(dot_member_call(routine operator=, var b2, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(var b){const UA:Lg}){const UA &:g}){UA &}){UA:Lgu}`;
`UC` (user copy constructor) `:16` `dik_constructor ... routine=UC args=reference_to(lvalue_adjust(var c)) is_implicit_copy_for_copy_initialization=TRUE`; `VF` (virtual) `:21` `dot_member_call(routine operator={VF &(*)(const VF &) noexcept}, ...)`, an
implicit operator that is not trivial. **H2: the expression alone does not prove triviality of the class**: `DT` (user destructor, `:17-18`), `Der` (a base, `:19-20`), `DefA` (defaulted `operator=`, `:22`) and `WithMem` (`:23`) are copied by plain `eok_assign` / `dik_expression: var`, so the class-level test of item 1 is the guard; the shape
`eok_assign` with `operation.type_kind: tk_struct` is only the necessary half.

**6. `sizeof` and `offsetof`: PASS; folded in every position, both modes.** `z1.c:5-13` (`struct S { int x; char c; struct T t; struct S *next; }`): `init a: dik_constant: const[int 24UL]{unsigned long}` for `sizeof(struct S)` (:5), `sizeof s` (:6), `sizeof *p` (:11); `offsetof(struct S, t)` (:7) `8UL`,
