`... const[int 4UL]`. Both `_Static_assert`s of `z1.c:16-17` pass. These are EDG's ABI sizes (24 for five members), not the model's: see N5.

**H3 (mode difference, as P64's `&*q`):** the macro `cerastes_old(e)` is `(*(__typeof__(e)*)cerastes_old_(&(e)))`; for `old(*s)` the front end folds `&(*s)` to `s` in C23 (`cast(param_ref 1)`) and keeps `address_of(indirect(param_ref 1))` in C++20
(`k2.c:11`, `:26`, `:29` differ only there). **So `old(*p).x` is the same place as `old(p->x)` as a fact, and it is decidable from the IL, but the tree differs**: the argument of `cerastes_old_` is the whole `*p`
(a bare parameter or `address_of(indirect(param))`), and the member path is the `dot_field` chain outside the `indirect(cast(call(...)))`. `old(s->t).x` is the same with `address_of(points_to_field(param, t))` inside and
a `dot_field` outside. Record 0043 item 9 may therefore accept `old(*p).x` (peel the chain, then fold the path) or keep rejecting it; both are implementable.

**C++ spellings (`k3.cpp`, probe line = b-number + 4; same places):** `cerastes::owns(*s)` is `call(routine owns, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(indirect(param_ref 1))))`, `owns(s->x)` `reference_to(lvalue_adjust(points_to_field(param_ref 1, field x)))`,
`owns(s->t.x)` `reference_to(lvalue_adjust(dot_field(points_to_field(...), field x)))`, `live(s)` `call(routine live, cast(param_ref 1))`; `old(s->x)` is `ref_indirect(call(routine old, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(points_to_field(param_ref 1, field x)))))`,
`old(*s).x` (`k3.cpp:11`) `dot_field(ref_indirect(call(routine old, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(indirect(param_ref 1))))), field x)`, `old(*s).t.x` (:15) a `dot_field(dot_field(ref_indirect(...), t), x)`, `old(s->t).x` (:14) with `points_to_field(param_ref 1, field t)` inside. The wrappers
`reference_to(lvalue_adjust(...))` and `ref_indirect(...)` are the ones the existing walker already peels for scalars (P53).
**Promotion of scalar members** (`k4.c:5`, `struct S { char c; short sh; bool b; enum E e; unsigned u; }`): `owns(s->c)`, `reads(s->b)`, `owns(s->sh)` come as `cast(points_to_field(param_ref 1, field c){char<-same}){int:g}` (`compiler_generated` promotion cast around the member place, as P53 found for `*p`);
`owns(s->e)` has the cast in C++20 only; `owns(s->u)` none; the same casts appear around `s->c` in `s->c == cerastes_old(s->c)` and around the `old` result. The existing "strip `compiler_generated` casts around a place" rule covers it.

`void m1(struct S *p CERASTES_REF_TO_UNINIT)` (:5), `m2 ... CERASTES_MUST_INIT` (:7), `m3(struct S *p CERASTES_OWNING)` (:9), `m4(CERASTES_OWNING struct S *p)` (:10), `m5(... CERASTES_MUST_INIT CERASTES_OWNING)` (:11), `m8(struct S **pp CERASTES_OWNING)` (:15), `m9` (:16), `m10(struct S *p CERASTES_MUST_INIT)`
with `CERASTES_REQUIRES(cerastes_owns(p->t))` (:17-18). The walker and `ilsum` show `[[cerastes::ref_to_uninit]]`, `must_init`, `owning` with `loc=declarator-id` (trailing) or `loc=prefix` (leading `m4`), two attribute blocks each (P64 A), the
function type printing `void (struct S *)`; `m5` carries both markers. EDG accepts all of them on a `struct S *` and `struct S **` parameter. **`CERASTES_UNINIT` on a struct local is accepted** in both modes, leading (`mk1.c:13` `CERASTES_UNINIT struct S s;`) and trailing the declarator
(`:14` `struct S s CERASTES_UNINIT;`): the variable's `attributes` is non-NULL (`variable s ... attributes: file-scope attribute@...`), `init_kind: initk_none`, and the walker prints `attr [[cerastes::uninit]] on variable s @ L13:17` and `@ L14:28`. Placed between the type and the declarator

**9. Struct pointers: PASS; the shapes of P51 with a struct pointee.** `sp1.c` (both modes; `struct S **pp`, results, comparisons, conversions):
```
:8  struct S *a = &s;      init a: address_of(var s{struct S:L}){struct S *}          s and a: address_taken=TRUE (:9 pp = &a)
:9  struct S **pp = &a;    init pp: address_of(var a{struct S *:L}){struct S **}
:10 struct S *b = *pp;     init b: indirect(var pp{struct S **<-same}){struct S *<-same}
:11 *pp = p;               assign(indirect(var pp){struct S *:L}, var p){struct S *:u}
:12 p == NULL              eq(var p, const[int 0]{struct S * is_simple_zero implicit_cast explicit_cast_applied null_pointer_constant_ruled_out}){int}   (:13 ne, :14 not(var p){int})
:15 (int *)&s              cast(address_of(var s{struct S:L}){struct S *}){int *}           (explicit: not compiler_generated)
:16 (struct T *)p          cast(var p{struct S *<-same}){struct T *}
:17 void *vp = p;          cast(var p){void *:g}      :18 (void *)p  cast(var p){void *}      :19 (struct S *)vp  cast(var vp{void *<-same}){struct S *}

:23 p == b                 eq(var p, var b){int};   :24 p->next  points_to_field(var p, field next{struct S *}){struct S *<-same};   :25 s.next = &s  assign(dot_field(var s, field next){struct S *:L}, address_of(var s))
```

C++ wraps comparisons and `!` in `cast(...){int:g}` over a `bool` as P51 item 5. A `struct S *` result is a pointer-typed `return` and call result exactly like `int *` (`sp1.c:4-5`, `:22`).

**What the encoder reads (summary).**
- Struct type: `kind tk_struct|tk_class|tk_union`, `incomplete`, `is_local_to_function`, `field_list` (index k = position in the `next` chain), per field `type` (strip `tk_typeref`, noting `qualifiers`; `tk_array`, `tk_pointer` + `is_reference`/pointee kind `tk_void`/`tk_routine`, `tk_struct`, `tk_union`), `is_bit_field`, `is_anonymous_parent_object`; class: `is_empty_class`, `is_packed`; system file by `seq_is_in_system_header(decl_position.seq)`; C++: `base_classes`, `any_virtual_functions`, `has_field_initializer`, the `assoc_scope` `variables` (static members) and `routines` (all `compiler_generated` and trivial) and the member `access`.
- Access: `eok_dot_field`, `eok_points_to_field` (operand 2 = `enk_field`, `field` = the `a_field`), nested by operand 1; `(*p).x` is `dot_field(indirect(p))`; `address_of` over either; no casts; the lvalue flag only on write positions and intermediates.
- Initializer: `variable.dynamic` (`dik_constant` | `dik_nonconstant_aggregate` | `dik_expression` for a copy | `dik_constructor` rejected) over `ck_aggregate` elements in source order with `ck_designator` (field pointer) elements, nested aggregates for elided braces and designator paths, unmentioned trailing members absent, C++ fillers without `decl_position`.
- Copy: `eok_assign` with `operation.type_kind: tk_struct`, `dik_expression` of a struct-typed source; anything else (`dot_member_call` of `operator=`, `dik_constructor`) is the non-trivial case.
- Contracts: places are `indirect(p)`, `points_to_field`, `dot_field(points_to_field ...)`, `dot_field(indirect ...)`, wrapped in `cast{g}` (scalar members, C), `reference_to(lvalue_adjust(...))` (C++), and for `old` in `indirect(cast(call(cerastes_old_, ...)))` / `ref_indirect(call(old, ...))` with the member path outside for `old(*p).path`.

**Hazards (the encoder must handle; none contradicts an item of the plan).**
- **H1** C++20 designated lists carry compiler-generated zero fillers (item 4); a duplicate-designator check must ignore them, and the cursor rule must be the semantics.
- **H2** The class-level test, not the copy expression, guards triviality (item 5); a class with a user destructor, a base or a defaulted `operator=` is copied by plain `eok_assign`.
- **H3** `old(*p)` folds `&*p` in C23 and not in C++20 (item 7).
- **H4** In C++20 each struct adds two implicit routines to the file: `routine T::operator= plain implicit nobody @ L1:8` for the copy and the move assignment (`--cerastes_walk m2.c --c++20` lists four for two structs; `ilsum` `ROUTINE L1 operator= : T &(const T &) defined=FALSE`; `compiler_generated=TRUE`, `is_trivial_copy_function=TRUE`). Every loop over the file's routines (the walker prints them, an encoder pass over uncalled declarations would reach them) must skip routines with `compiler_generated`; in C there are none.
- **H5** `typedef struct { ... } Pt;` has no tag in C23 (`ty1.c:1` `TYPE ?`), and C++20 names it `Pt` (`TYPE Pt`): a name for `ptr_struct_<n>_<tag>` and `alloc_struct_<n>_<tag>` needs a fallback to the typedef name or to `n` in C (`Pt` is a `tk_typeref` named `Pt` whose `typeref_type` is `struct <unnamed@...>`, `ty1.c:1`), or the two modes name the same program differently.
- **H6** EDG diagnoses out-of-order and repeated designators with `#2904-D` in both modes (and the usual `#177`/`#550`); tests that use them carry a warning on their lines.

**Notes.**
- **N1** `__attribute__((packed))` (`is_packed`, type :10636 and field :11954) is not in item 2's rejection list; the model's `&p->i` of a packed member is a misaligned pointer. Recommend rejecting packed structs (M8) in item 2.
- **N2** `contains_flexible_array_member` (il_def.h:10622) is not printed by `il_display`; a flexible member is recognised by the last member's incomplete array type, and the encoder (in process) can read the flag.
- **N3** `_Atomic` members have no class flag; only the member's typeref `qualifiers: _Atomic`. `const`/`volatile` have both.
- **N4** Anonymous members are `is_anonymous_parent_object` on the field; the *struct* type they hold also prints `is_nonstd_anonymous_union_type` (a GNU C struct), so test the field, not the member's kind. A named member of an unnamed struct type is a plain nested struct (`ty1.c:3`).
- **N5** `sizeof(struct S)` and `offsetof` fold to EDG's ABI values (24 for `struct S` of `z1.c`), which are unrelated to the model's member blocks: `malloc(sizeof(struct S))` (M4.5d2) must size by the model, not by this constant.
- **N6** il_def.h line numbers in the plan text: `eok_dot_field` is :14181 and `eok_points_to_field` :14185 at the pinned fork commit (the plan cites 14174/14178).
- **N7** Struct pointers to an incomplete struct are legal parameters and locals (`inc1.c:7`); only a dereference or an object is an EDG error (#70/#833), so the encoder sees only the pointer.
- **N8** C: `struct S {}` has size 0 and C++ size 1 (both `is_empty_class`); a plain C `Empty` is already rejected by item 2.
- **N9** `{0}` for a struct whose first member is a struct (`i4.c:6`) expands through the elided braces (`aggr{aggr{0}[T]}`), so "zero-fill the unmentioned members" must recurse into nested structs and pointers (null) for every absent trailing element, in both modes.

### P66: compiler matrix of member sequencing shapes and uninitialized struct use (record 0043 items 6, 7, 12; test-mutator)

Evidence: `build/m4.5c1/p66/` (`gen.py` regenerates `src/`, `raw/<shape>.<compiler-mode>.<tier>.<syntax|O2>.txt` and `results.json`; the table below is built from `results.json`).
Versions: Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2, `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/clang` and `clang++`), arm64-apple-darwin27.0.0; Homebrew GCC 16.2.0 (`gcc-16`, `g++-16`).
Modes `-std=c23` (C) and `-std=c++20` (C++); tiers D (no flag), A (`-Wall`), E (`-Wall -Wextra`); `-fsyntax-only` everywhere, and `-O2 -c -o /dev/null` (the flow warnings) for all four compilers at every tier.
Each shape is one function over `struct S { int x; int y; }; struct T { struct S t; int z; };`. M shapes: `int r = <expr>; (void)s; return r;` with `struct S s = {0, 0};` (M9/M10 `struct T s = {{0, 0}, 0};`; M6-M8 take `struct S *p, struct S *q` as parameters), so the only warnings are the shape's own. U shapes: `int f(void)` with the listed body.
The matrix reports only warnings; no shape produced an error and no warning lacked a flag.

#### For the owner

- **Clang is silent on every M shape, in both modes at every tier** (`-Wunsequenced` names objects syntactically, P61, and does not see a member access: `s.x + (s.x = 1)` and `x++ + x` differ here). GCC's `-Wsequence-point` warns at `-Wall` (A, E; never at D) in **both** modes, `-fsyntax-only` and `-O2` alike, on every shape that names one member object twice with a write: M1, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M9.
- **No compiler warns** on M2 `s.x + (s.y = 1)`, M7 `p->x + (q->x = 1)` and M10 `s.t.x + (s.t.y = 1)`: different members of one object, or two pointers (the path-precise `unsequenced` check is their only coverage, 0039 item 3).
- By the union rule of 0039 item 3 (a warning at no flag or `-Wall` in some compiler and mode): **M1, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M9 are `unsequenced_modification` rejections** (the plan's twin `s.x + (s.x = 1)` is one: the plan's "if P66 shows a warning" holds, by GCC at `-Wall` only); M2, M7, M10 are accepted; M7 is `unsequenced` path-precisely when `p == q` is possible. Nothing in M is `-Wextra`-only. `-O2` changes nothing. `p->x` twice (M6, M8) and `s.t.x` twice (M9) are named objects like `*p` and `s.x`: object keys with member paths (record 0043 item 12).
- **Uninitialized use** (U): the whole-struct copy of an unset struct (U1) warns in clang C only at `-Wall` (`-Wuninitialized`, both `-fsyntax-only` and `-O2`; clang C++ is silent); GCC warns only with `-O2` (`-Wall` and up; `-fsyntax-only` is silent). The read of an unset member (U3, U4) warns in GCC at `-Wall -O2` only; clang never. **U2 (copy of a partly initialized struct) warns nowhere**: cerastes's `uninitialized` at that copy (question 92: a copy reads every member) is stricter than every compiler. It is an error category, not a rejection, so the union rule does not apply.
- **EDG itself** (`scripts/cpfe.sh --c23` / `--c++20 --no_code_gen`, stock): silent on every M shape except `#550` (variable set but never used) on M4 in C++ only; warns `#549` ("variable `s` is used before its value is set") on U1 and U3 in both modes; silent on U2 and U4. The M shapes therefore reach the back end without a front-end diagnostic, as in P61/A8.

#### Matrix

Cell = flag and the first tier that warns; `(-O2 only)` = silent under `-fsyntax-only`. Columns: clang C, clang C++, GCC C, GCC C++.

| Shape | Source | clang-C | clang-C++ | gcc-C | gcc-C++ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `s.x + (s.x = 1)` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M2 | `s.x + (s.y = 1)` | silent | silent | silent | silent |
| M3 | `s.x++ + s.x` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M4 | `(s.x = 1) + (s.x = 2)` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M5 | `s.x = s.x++` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M6 | `p->x + (p->x = 1)` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M7 | `p->x + (q->x = 1)` | silent | silent | silent | silent |
| M8 | `p->x = p->x++` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M9 | `s.t.x + (s.t.x = 1)` | silent | silent | `-Wsequence-point` from A | `-Wsequence-point` from A |
| M10 | `s.t.x + (s.t.y = 1)` | silent | silent | silent | silent |
| U1 | `struct S s; struct S t = s; return t.x;` | `-Wuninitialized` from A | silent | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) |
| U2 | `struct S s; s.x = 1; struct S t = s; return t.x;` | silent | silent | silent | silent |
| U3 | `struct S s; return s.y;` | silent | silent | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) |
| U4 | `struct S s; s.x = 1; return s.y;` | silent | silent | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) | `-Wuninitialized` from A (`-O2` only) |

#### Classification

- **Reject (`unsequenced_modification`):** M1, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M9 (GCC `-Wall`, both modes).
- **Accept; `unsequenced` by path:** M7 (`p`/`q` may alias); M2 and M10 need no check (distinct member objects).
- **U1-U4:** all accepted by the front end; U1, U3 (EDG `#549`) and U4 are `uninitialized` errors by 0019/0043 (a read of a leaf whose flag is false); U2 is `uninitialized` at the copy by question 92 only.

### S33: Silicon on record 0043's shapes (nested allocation, leaf overlap, loop liveness, copies, `must_init` over a struct, member-address `WF`) **PASS for (a)-(g); every vacuity run fails as it must; one completeness finding (g), answered by item 8's `WF_S`**

Evidence: `tests/viper-smoke/memory/s33_*.vpr` (22 files: a positive and a twin per case, and one `_vacuity_fail` per case), hand-written by test-mutator in the emitted style (the four axioms with their tags, one assert per atomic check, ghost `Perm` amounts, trusted `alloc_struct_0_S` and `alloc_struct_1_T`); generator in `build/m4.5c1/s33/`. Each passes `python3 scripts/run_tests.py <file>` alone (5–16 s each, the vacuity files about 15 s). Silicon never failed first with its own reason.

- **(a) nested allocation** (`struct T { struct S s; int z; }`): the allocation's root facts, every member block's `len == 1`, every leaf uninitialized; writes and reads of `t.s.x`, `t.z`; `&t.s` to a callee owning `*s`; the scope exit (every leaf and the liveness cell at `write`, exhaled). Twin: the read of the unwritten `t.z` fails at its flag assert.
- **(b) the leaf-overlap trap:** `f(&s, &t.x)` against `requires owns(*s) && owns(*q)` (S's leaves, an `int`) verifies; `f(&s, &s.x)` fails at the caller's explicit `assert q != loc(member(s, 0), 0)`, the only error. Control: without that assert Silicon fails first at the call with its own `insufficient.permission` (exit 3 territory): the explicit separation by leaf is what keeps it out.
- **(c) nested overlap:** `g(&t, &u.s)` verifies; `g(&t, &t.s)` fails at `assert s != loc(member(t, 0), 0)`, the only error (the same control).
- **(d) loop liveness:** one `acc(lvloc(block_of(s)).lv, kl)` row per root block verifies; one row per leaf fails on entry (`invariant-entry:insufficient.permission`, the second row: twice the snapshot amount over one cell).
- **(e) copies:** read every source leaf (permission, flag) into temporaries, then write every destination leaf (flag set): `t = s` and the exact self-copy `*p = *p` (also through a call) verify; a source leaf with its flag false fails at its flag assert. A fresh cell has no range fact, so the twin calls nothing after the copy.
- **(f) `must_init` over a struct:** the leaves' permissions without flags on entry, every leaf's flag promised; writing both verifies, writing one fails at the return row of the other's flag.
- **(g) member-address `WF`:** `&p->y` = `loc(member(p, 1), 0)` passed to a callee with `requires WF(q)` and `owns(*q)` verifies when the caller's atom states `len(member(p, 1)) == 1`; with only `live(p)`, or the leaf permissions without the length facts, `WF(q)` fails — only its conjunct `offset_of(q) <= len(block_of(q))` (the others follow from `loc_inv`). So record 0043 item 8's `WF_S` carries the member lengths with every struct pointer (`live(p)` included).
- **(h) vacuity:** each method cloned with `assert false` at its start and end, after each allocation and after each call: every one fails at its expected line (a 5, b 5, c 5, d 3, e 6, f 5, g 5 errors).
- **Controls:** a wrong value in (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) fails exactly there; dropping the loop's `ds ==> flag` row in (d) fails the read after the loop.

  aggregate), `:5` `return S{1, {2}};` `dik_constant is_braced_initializer is_explicit_cast: aggr{...}[S ... explicit_cast_applied]`, `:6` `return S();` `dik_zero is_explicit_cast`
  (no aggregate), `:7` `return S{};` `dik_constant ... is_partially_initialized is_explicit_cast: aggr{}`. Scalar returns in C++ keep `expr` (`q1.c:9`). `il_def.h:16745`
  `return_dynamic_init` is documented for "a copy constructor (C++ only)"; for these trivial classes it is non-NULL anyway and `expr` is NULL (`:16592-16597`). **The reader of `return` must
  take `expr` or `return_dynamic_init` (its `dik_expression`/`dik_constant`/`dik_zero` forms), in C++ for every class-typed return.**
- **H2. C++ folds compound-literal values that C leaves as `temp_init`.** `q4.c:4` `return (struct S){1, 2}.x;` is `dot_field(temp_init[...]{struct S:L}, field x)` in C23 and
  `const[int 1]{int null_pointer_constant_ruled_out}` in C++20; `q4.c:14` `(int){5} + (int){6}` is `add(temp_init[...5], temp_init[...6])` in C23 and `dik_constant: const[int 11]` in C++20
  (the whole initializer folded); `q4.c:10` `struct S s = (struct S){1, 2};` is `dik_expression: temp_init[dik_constant is_braced_initializer is_compound_literal: aggr]` in C23
  and a plain `dik_constant: aggr{1, 2}[S explicit_braces_on_aggregate]` in C++20. The folds happen only when the whole expression is constant; `q4.c:9` `t = (struct S){1, 2};` keeps its
  `temp_init` in both modes, `q4.c:5` `return (int){5};` too. **The reader must accept both shapes and the folded constant.**
- **H3. EDG gives no diagnostic for `&(S){1, 2}` in C++ (or `&(int){5}`), and `return &(int){5};` is only warned in C.** `q4x.cpp:7` `S *p = &(S){1, 2};`, `:10` `int *p = &(int){5};`, `:11`
  `h(&(S){1, 2});`: exit 0, no message beyond `#550-D`; the IL is the C shape (`address_of(temp_init[... is_compound_literal ...]{S:L})`). `q4.c:16` `return &(int){5};` warns `#1057-D returning
  pointer to local temporary` in C23 and says nothing in C++20 (`q4.c.c++20.diag`). **The C++ rejection of item 7 (and R14's return rule) must be the encoder's own: nothing in the front end stops
  either.**
- **H4. A block-scope compound literal has no variable or scope entity; only its enclosing statement says where it lives, and C wraps its control statements in a compiler-generated block.**
  Zero `a_variable` blocks of `is_compound_literal` in `q4.c` (both modes) and `q2c.c` (C23), by a scan of the `.il` files. In C23 every `if`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `switch` is
  `block (compiler_generated) > <statement>` (`q4g.c:2-3` `if (a) {...}` and `while`, even without a literal; `q4h.c:1` `switch`; `q4g.c:5` `do ... while`, `:7` `for`); C++20 has no such block
  (`q4g.c.c++20.sum` `k1` is `if` directly under the function block). A non-compound substatement of an `if` is a `block (compiler_generated)` in both modes (`q4g.c:4` `if (a) h(&(int){a});`).
  A literal in the controlling expression is a child of the `if`/`while`/`for`/`switch` statement's `expr` (or the `for`'s `increment`), under C23's wrapping block (`q4.c:11` `c8`, `:12` `c9`, `:18` `c15`
  `increment: assign(var i, add(indirect(address_of(temp_init[...]{int:L})), const 1))`). **The lifetime of the object of item 7 follows the nearest enclosing `stmk_block`; in C that
  block is the generated one around the control statement, so the plan's `{Decl; If}` shape is what EDG already shows.**
- **H5. Which compound literals EDG makes static variables.** `q4d.c:1` `int *gp = &(int){5};` (file scope): `gp` is `initk_static` with a `ck_address` constant, `abk_variable`, `address.offset 0`, whose `variable` is a
  compiler-generated unnamed `a_variable` (`storage_class: sc_static`, `address_taken: TRUE`, `compiler_generated: TRUE`, `is_compound_literal: TRUE`, `init_kind: initk_static`, constant `(int)5`, `declared_type: NULL`),
  both modes (`q4d.c.c23.il:2466-2481`, `a_variable.is_compound_literal` `il_def.h:11621`: "generated by the front end to hold a static compound literal"). `q4e.c:2` `struct S gs = (struct S){1, 2};` (file scope)
  is accepted in both modes and is a plain `initk_static` aggregate `aggr{1, 2}[... explicit_braces_on_aggregate]` with no variable of its own, but its `ck_aggregate` constant carries `is_compound_literal: TRUE` (`q4e.c.c23.il`, raw field; `ilsum` does not print it; `a_constant.is_compound_literal` `il_def.h:4951`). No `a_variable` is made for a block-scope literal.
- **H6. C and C++ differ in the zero fillers of a literal and in `S()`.** `q2c.c:4` `(struct S){.y = a}`: C23 `aggr{desig(.y), dyn(var a)}` (`x` absent), C++20 `aggr{const[int 0]{int}, desig(.y), dyn(var a)}` (P65 H1 again). `S()` is
  `temp_init[dik_zero is_explicit_cast has_temporary_lifetime is_functional_notation_cast]` (`q2x.cpp:5`, `q5x.cpp:6`, `q3x.cpp:6`) with no aggregate at all, while the same `S()` as an initializer of a variable is
  `dik_constant is_explicit_cast: aggr{const[int 0]{int null_pointer_constant_ruled_out}, const[int 0]{...}}[S explicit_cast_applied]` (`q5x.cpp:3`, global `q6x.cpp:8`); `S{}` is `aggr{}[... is_partially_initialized]`.
  **A zero-fill must handle `dik_zero` as every leaf zero.**
- **H7. The C++ `S{...}` of an initializer or a return is not a `temp_init`; of an assignment or an argument it is.** `q5x.cpp:2` `S s = S{1, 2};` is `dik_constant: aggr{1, 2}[S explicit_braces_on_aggregate implicit_cast
  explicit_cast_applied]` (no `is_braced_initializer` on the dynamic-init); `q5x.cpp:5` `t = S{1, 2};`, `q2x.cpp:4` `g(S{1, 2});`, `q3x.cpp:14` `*p = S{1, {2}};` are `temp_init[dik_constant is_braced_initializer is_explicit_cast
  has_temporary_lifetime: aggr{...}[S ... explicit_cast_applied] is_functional_notation_cast source.type=S]` (`dynamic_init` `il_def.h:15394-15408`, `has_temporary_lifetime` `:4093`, `is_explicit_cast` `:4145`,
  `is_functional_notation_cast` `:14997`, `source.type` `:15410`), `g({1, 2});` (`q2x.cpp:8`) the same without `is_explicit_cast` and without a position (`{S:}`). A non-constant element stays `dyn(dik_expression: ...)` under
  `dik_nonconstant_aggregate ... non_constant` (`q5x.cpp:8` `t = S{a, a++}`, `q2x.cpp:9`).
- **H8. In C++ a `const` class source gets `eok_lvalue_adjust`; C carries the const only in `orig_lvalue_type`.** `q2d.c:3` `g(*p)` with `const struct S *p`: C23 `indirect(var p){struct S<-const struct S}`, C++20 `lvalue_adjust(indirect(var p){const S:L}){S<-same:g}`;
  the same for `var s` of a `const` parameter (`q2d.c:5`) and for a copy initializer (`:4`). A non-const source has neither (`q2.c:6`). C++ prints a `const` by-value parameter's function type without the top-level `const` (`void (S)`), C keeps it (`void (const struct S)`).
- **H9. `&h.x` as a global initializer is the same address as `&h` unless `subobject_path` is read.** `q6.c:12` `struct P g7 = {&h2.x, 1}` is `const[addr abk_variable h2 off=0]` with a non-NULL `subobject_path` and the constant's type `int *` with
  `implicit_cast` (`q6.c:23` `int *gp16 = &h2.y;` is `off=4`, also `subobj`); `q6.c:11` `{&h, 1}` is `off=0` and no `subobject_path`. (`a_constant.address.subobject_path` `il_def.h:5219`.) Item 8 rejects `&h.x`: the test is `subobject_path != NULL` or the
  constant's type against the variable's (P63 H3, H5), never `offset != 0`.

| `extern "C" S g9 = {1, 2};` (`q6x.cpp:14-15`) | linkage `C` in C++20 |

The leaf index of a `ck_address` initializer is positional in `aggr{...}` as in P65 item 4; `init_kind` (`il_def.h:11747`), `a_variable.declared_type` `:11814`, `a_constant.kind ck_address` `:3645`, `ck_aggregate` `:3661`.

#### 7. `decreases(p->x)` and `decreases(g.x)`: PASS

`q7.c:7` `CERASTES_DECREASES(p->x)` (a pointer parameter `struct S *p`): `points_to_field(param_ref 1 up=0{struct S *<-same}, field x{int}){int:L}`; `q7.c:12` `decreases(g.x)`: `dot_field(var g{struct S:L}, field x{int}){int:L}`; `q7.c:16` `decreases(s.x)` (by value): `dot_field(param_ref 1 up=0{struct S:L}, field x{int}){int:L}`. The measure operand is an **lvalue** (`{int:L}`),
while the same member in a `requires` is a value `{int<-same}` (`q7.c:5`, `:10`, `:15`: `ge(points_to_field(param_ref 1 up=0, field x){int<-same}, const 0)`, `ge(dot_field(var g{struct S:L}, field x){int<-same}, 0)`). `owns(g)` is `call(routine cerastes_owns, var g{struct S<-same})` (an rvalue `var g`, `q7.c:10`);
`owns(*p)` is `call(routine cerastes_owns, indirect(param_ref 1 up=0{struct S *<-same}){struct S<-same})`. Same in both modes except the `bool` types.

#### Notes

- **N1.** `ilsum.py` ran into a cycle on `switch` bodies (the case statements point back); `_seen` and a depth cap were added; nothing in the IL is affected.
- **N2.** `(int){5}` as a value is `temp_init` over a `ck_integer` and under `&` is an lvalue `{int:L}` (item 4); a literal in an initializer of a local `int` in C++ is folded to the constant (`q4.c:14` `x = 11`).
- **N3.** `struct S gs = (struct S){1, 2};` at file scope is accepted by EDG although ISO C requires a constant initializer, and it is an ordinary `initk_static` aggregate (H5); record 0044 item 7 rejects file-scope literals, so the global reader must reject a `ck_aggregate` constant with `is_compound_literal: TRUE` (raw field, set here; `ilsum` does not print it) and the `&(int){5}` form (a `ck_address` whose `variable` has `is_compound_literal`), or it accepts both as plain initial values.
- **N4.** Expression positions (`@Lline:col`) of a `temp_init` are those of the opening `(` or of the type name of the literal; a C++ `{1, 2}` in an argument or assignment has no position (`{S:}`), so a message about it falls back to the enclosing statement.
- **N5.** Not probed: a literal inside a lambda or a statement expression, `static`/`thread_local` struct locals in C++ with a dynamic initializer beyond `q6x.cpp:16`, and `restrict` by-value structs (no IL content).

### P68: compiler matrix of struct-value shapes (record 0044 items 5-7, 9; test-mutator)

Evidence: `build/m4.5c2a/p68/` (`gen.py` regenerates `src/`, `raw/<shape>.<compiler-mode>.<tier>.<syntax|O2>.txt`, `raw/<shape>.EDG-<c|cpp>.txt` and `results.json`; `table.py` builds `table.md` below from `results.json`).
Versions: Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2, `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/clang` and `clang++`), arm64-apple-darwin27.0.0; Homebrew GCC 16.2.0 (`gcc-16`, `g++-16`); EDG: the stock `build/edg/bin/cpfe` through `scripts/cpfe.sh` (`--c23` / `--c++20 --no_code_gen`).
Method as P66: modes `-std=c23` (C) and `-std=c++20` (C++), tiers D (no flag), A (`-Wall`), E (`-Wall -Wextra`), each with `-fsyntax-only` and with `-O2 -c -o /dev/null` (the flow warnings): 900 compiler runs. A shape valid in both languages is the same source in both modes (`struct S` spelled out; C++ only shapes use `S{...}`/`(S){...}`). Shapes that only one language accepts are `-` in the other column.
Cell = the first tier at which any diagnostic appears, with the flag (`-O2 only` = silent under `-fsyntax-only`); `ERROR` = the compiler refuses; `silent` = nothing at any tier, either way of running. Declarations: `struct S { int x; int y; }; struct T { struct S t; int z; };`, `get(struct S)`, `h(struct S, int)`, `h2(struct S, struct S)`; M-like shapes are `int r = <expr>; (void)s; return r;` with `struct S s = {0, 0};`.
The union rule of 0020 item 5 / 0039 item 3 (rejected like the compilers): a warning at tier D or A, `-fsyntax-only`, in some compiler and mode.

#### For the owner

- **Sequencing with a struct argument.** Only `h2(s, s = t)` (Q4: the argument `s` and the assignment `s = t` name the whole object) warns: clang `-Wunsequenced` at no flag (C only; clang++ is silent), GCC `-Wsequence-point` from `-Wall` in both modes. By the union rule Q4 is an `unsequenced_modification` rejection. `get(s) + (s.y = 1)`, `get(s) + s.x++`, `h(s, s.x = 1)` and `h(s, s.y++)` (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5) are silent in every compiler, mode and tier (a by-value argument is a read of the whole `s`, which the compilers do not connect to a member write): they are accepted by the union rule. they are accepted by the compiler union rule. Record 0044 item 5 rejects them anyway (`unsequenced_modification`, 0039 item 3's static rule, question 70): a by-value argument reads every leaf of `s` (question 97), so each shape reads and writes one leaf, which C leaves undefined (C23 6.5p2), although no compiler connects the member write to the whole-object argument.
- **Compound literal assignments** (L1-L6): silent everywhere, in both languages and at every tier, including `s = (struct S){s.x++, 0}` and `s = (struct S){.x = (s.y = 1), .y = 2}` and C++'s `s = S{s.x++, 0}`: no compiler diagnoses an element that writes the destination, so the C rule of record 0044 item 6 (a destination no element names, whose address is not taken) is cerastes's own, not "like the compilers"; the harmless swap `s = (struct S){s.y, s.x}` is silent too. Nothing here is a union-rule rejection.
- **`-Wmissing-field-initializers`** is `-Wextra`-only in every compiler and mode (W1-W4, W6): `(struct S){1}`, `struct S g = {1};`, `return (struct S){1};` and `S{1}` warn from tier E, never at D or A; accepted by the union rule. `{0}` is silent in C but warns in C++ with both compilers (W5: `missing initializer for member 'S::y'`); `S{}` is silent (W7).
- **C++ compound literals** `(S){1, 2}` as a value, an initializer, an argument or an assignment source (K1, K2, K4) are silent in clang++ and g++ at every tier (they warn only under `-pedantic`, not measured). **`&(S){1, 2}` is an error in both** (K3, R1-R5, C3, C4 in C++): clang `-Waddress-of-temporary` (an error by default) or `cannot take the address of an rvalue of type 'int'`, GCC `taking address of rvalue [-fpermissive]` or `lvalue required as unary '&' operand`. **EDG accepts them silently** in C++ (K3, C3, C4; R1/R3 only warn `returning pointer to local temporary`), so cerastes must reject `&(S){...}` in C++ itself (the two new C++ pins of the flips).
- **Escaping a compound literal's address** in C: `return &(int){5};` (R1, R3) warns in clang at no flag (`-Wreturn-stack-address`) and in GCC only with `-O2` (`-Wreturn-local-addr`; silent under `-fsyntax-only`): already 0039 item 6's R14. Through a pointer variable (R2 block, R4 loop, R5 `if` condition) clang is silent at every tier and GCC warns only with `-O2` from `-Wall` (`-Wdangling-pointer=`, plus a `-Wuninitialized` on the literal); not a union-rule rejection under `-fsyntax-only`, so these are cerastes's `lifetime` errors (the H3 twins), not rejections. EDG warns only on the direct `return` (R1, R3).
- **C23 storage-class literals and file-scope literals:** `(static int){5}` and `(constexpr int){5}` (C1, C2, C5): **clang 21 refuses both** (`expected expression`), **GCC 16 accepts both silently**, and **EDG refuses both** (`a storage class may not be specified here`; `constexpr` is an undefined identifier, as handoff 8's C23 `constexpr` entry says): record 0044 item 7's rejection of them is unreachable, the front end errors first (a `frontend-error`-style outcome). File-scope `int *gp = &(int){5};` and `struct S *gq = &(struct S){1, 2};` (C3, C4) are accepted silently by clang, GCC and EDG in C (static storage), errors in C++ (above): cerastes rejects them as a file-scope literal in both modes (item 7), by its own rule, not the compilers'.
- **Partly initialized struct by value:** `struct S s; s.x = 1; get(s);` (U1), `return s;` (U2) and the copy (U3) are silent in every compiler, mode, tier and `-O2`; only passing a struct with nothing set (U4) warns, in clang C at `-Wall` (`-Wuninitialized`; clang++ and GCC are silent) and in EDG (`variable "s" is used before its value is set`, both modes). cerastes's `uninitialized` at the call or return (question 97) is stricter than every compiler on U1 and U2 (an error category, not a rejection: the union rule does not apply).
- **Struct-valued calls in sequencing** (A1-A4: `h2(mk(), mk())`, `mk().x + mk().x`, `get(mk()) + g1`, `mk().x + (g1 = 3)` with `mk` writing the global `g1`): silent in every compiler, mode and tier (the calls are indeterminately sequenced, not unsequenced): accepted; cerastes's call-sequencing rules (0021, 0039) decide them as for scalar results.
- **C++ temporaries** (X1-X5: `S s = S{1, 2};`, `S s = S();`, `get(S{1, 2})`, `return S{};`, `mk().x`): silent everywhere.
- **EDG itself** is silent on every shape except `returning pointer to local temporary` (R1, R3, both modes), `#549` on U4 (both modes), the C23 refusals above; it accepts `&(S){...}` in C++ (clang and GCC do not).
- **Rejected by the union rule:** only Q4 (`h2(s, s = t)`, `unsequenced_modification`). By cerastes's own rule (record 0044 item 5) also Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5 and the named-destination literal shapes L1, L2, L5, L6; every other shape is accepted or is a path-precise error.

#### Classification

- **Reject (`unsequenced_modification`):** Q4 by the union rule (clang C at no flag, GCC from `-Wall`); Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5 and L1, L2, L5, L6 by cerastes's own rule (no compiler warns).
- **Accept:** L3, L4 (the swap), W1-W4, W6 (`-Wextra` only), K1, K2, K4 (C++ compound literals as values), A1-A4, X1-X5, C3, C4 in C.
- **Errors, not rejections:** U1-U4 (`uninitialized`, question 97, stricter than every compiler on U1 and U2); R2, R4, R5 (`lifetime`); R1, R3 (R14, `return_local_address`).
- **Rejected by cerastes itself (the front end or compilers disagree):** C++ `&(S){...}` and `&(int){5}` (K3, R1-R5, C3, C4 in C++: clang and GCC error, EDG accepts); C23 storage-class literals (C1, C2, C5: EDG errors first, clang errors, GCC accepts); file-scope literals in both modes (C3, C4).

### P69: the invariant heap-read gap (record 0044 item 12) **no wrong verdict, no exit 3; `p->q->x`, `*p->q` and `*gp` are accepted today and every twin fails for the right reason; `**pp` is rejected (exit 2); recommendation: accept and pin**

Evidence in `build/m4.5c2a/p69/` (not committed): the generators `gen.py` (the 24 programs of the plan's matrix), `gen2.py` (tautology twins for the unheld cases), `gen3.py` (vacuity pairs, first alias traps), `gen4.py` (bounded alias traps that repoint the loaded pointer) -
44 programs in all, each `.c`, never edited after generation; `run.sh <probe.c>...` (runs the **baseline** `m4.5c2a-base/build/cerastes verify <probe> --std=c23|c++20 --keep-vpr=out/<probe>.<mode>.vpr`, appends `results.tsv`: name, mode, exit status,
wall seconds, first line); `summarize.sh` (every error category with its line, from `out/*.out`). All runs 2026-11-02 with the baseline build (the session's starting commit), both modes on every program, 90 runs (one program twice): exit 0 x20, exit 1 x66, exit 2 x4, **exit 3 x0**. The
verdicts were identical in both modes in every program. Times 7-21 s each (up to 40 s for `a_trap2` C23) while the baseline suite and two other runs were using the machine. The category names are the tool's: `invariant-entry` (the plan wrote `invariant-established`),
`invariant-preserved`, `permission`, `termination`, `check`, `postcondition`, `overflow`.

Shapes (`CERASTES_INVARIANT` = inv, `CERASTES_DECREASES` = dec). The target of a loaded pointer is held by a **local** the function takes the address of (`struct L t; struct L s = {&t, 0}; struct L *p = &s;`), or by a static global in `main`.

| Shape | Program | Clause | Verdict (both modes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **(a) `p->q->x`**, `struct L { struct L *q; int x; }` | `a_inv_pos` | inv `... p == &s && p->q == &t && p->q->x == i` (body `t.x += 1`) | **verified** (exit 0) |
| | `a_vac_ok` / `a_vac_bad` | the same loop, `ensures r == n` / `r == n + 1` (`return t.x`) | verified / **error `postcondition`** @ L21 (not vacuous) |
| | `a_inv_val_est` | inv claims `p->q->x == i + 1` | **`invariant-entry`** @ L15 |
| | `a_inv_val_pres` | inv claims `p->q->x == 0`, body increments `t.x` | **`invariant-preserved`** @ L15 |
| | `a_inv_unheld` | `owns(*p)` only; inv `p->q->x == 0` | `invariant-entry` and **`permission`** @ L12 ("this loop invariant reads `(p->q)->x`, which this loop does not hold") |
| | `a_inv_unheld_taut`, `_nonull` | the same with the tautology `p->q->x == p->q->x` (and `p->q != 0` required) | **`permission`** @ L12 only |
| | `a_check_unheld` | a `CERASTES_CHECK(p->q->x == p->q->x)` outside any loop, for comparison | `permission` @ L11 ("reads `(p->q)->x` without owning it") |
| | `a_dec_pos` | dec `p->q->x - i` (`t.x == n`, body empty) | **verified** |
| | `a_dec_val` | dec `p->q->x` (constant) | **`termination`** @ L16 |
| | `a_dec_unheld` | dec `n - i + p->q->x * 0`, `owns(*p)` only | **`permission`** @ L13 ("this loop measure reads `(p->q)->x`") |
| | `a_trap` (unbounded `+=`) | inv `p->q->x == t.x`, `p` not pinned past `p == &s` | `overflow` @ L20 and `postcondition` @ L23 (an artifact of unbounded `int`; see `a_trap2`) |
| | `a_trap2` | the loop repoints `p->q = &u; u.x = 3`; inv `p->q->x == t.x` leaves the pointer free | **`invariant-preserved`** @ L17 (correct) |

**Findings.**
1. **No wrong verdict.** Every positive verifies (not vacuously: the postcondition or `check` twins fail), every value twin and every alias trap (the loop repoints the loaded pointer, or the invariant leaves it free) is an `error`, every unheld twin is a `permission` error at the clause's line, with the target named in source terms (`(p->q)->x`, `*p->q`, `*gp`). There is no exit 3 and no `internal_inconsistency`.
2. **The unheld twin is a `permission` error in all three shapes, but in (a) and (c) with a value claim it is a second error beside `invariant-entry`** (`a_inv_unheld`, `c_inv_unheld`); a test pinning only the permission failure needs a tautological claim (`p->q->x == p->q->x`, `*gp == *gp` with `gp != 0` required): `a_inv_unheld_taut`, `b_inv_unheld_taut`, `c_inv_unheld_taut2`.
3. **A loaded pointer the loop does not write keeps its value** (`c_trap_dec`): an invariant or a measure may read through it without pinning it, which is sound and agrees with 0041 item 10; one the loop writes is unknown at the start of an iteration unless the invariant pins it (`a_trap2`, `b_trap2`, `c_trap2`).
4. **The rejection of `**pp` stays syntactic:** `encode.cpp:3827` (`is_indirect_node(peel_place(ops[0]))`) fires for `**pp` in both clauses; the other three shapes reach `inv_deref` chains and are handled by the same held-place check as `*p` (its message names the chain). Item 12's "all verdicts right" branch applies: accept and pin the shapes below, extending 0040 item 5's N2 argument.
5. **Suggested pins** (each in both modes, one `expect:` each): `a_inv_pos` + `a_inv_val_pres` + `a_inv_unheld_taut` (`permission` @ L12); `b_inv_pos` + `b_inv_val_pres` + `b_inv_unheld_taut` (`@ L11`); `c_inv_pos` + `c_inv_val_pres` + `c_inv_unheld_taut2` (`@ L11`); the same three for a measure (`a_dec_pos`/`a_dec_val`/`a_dec_unheld`, `b_*`, `c_*`) and the alias traps `a_trap2`, `b_trap2`, `c_trap2`, `c_trap2_dec` (the traps are the probes that would catch an unsound accept; `c_trap_dec` as a positive that keeps `*gp` through an unwritten pointer).
6. **Not covered:** a loaded pointer to a heap block or to a caller's cell passed in (M4.5d2 has no `malloc` yet; `owns(*p->q)` atoms are M4.5c2b); `*s.q` of a by-value parameter (the shape item 12 says c2a makes reachable) was not probed here because the baseline rejects by-value struct parameters; it needs the c2a build.

### P70: the IL facts record 0045 relies on (places reached through a heap read: `**pp`, `***ppp`, `*gp`, `gp->x`, `p->q->x`, `*p->q`, `(*pp)->x`, `*s.q`, `*r.q`, `owns`/`reads`/`live`/`old`, function `decreases`, loop invariants and measures; qualifiers; today's verdicts) **PASS for Q1-Q4 as IL facts and verdicts; no stop condition of the plan (no level lost, no missing `eok_indirect`, no wrong verdict, no exit 3); sixteen HAZARDS (H1-H16) the encoder and the lowering must handle**

Evidence in `build/m4.5c2b/p70/` (not committed): generators `gen_il.py`, `gen_il2.py` (the IL probes, `il/*.c` for both modes and `il/*x.cpp` for the C++ spellings `cerastes::owns/reads/live/old`), `gen_v.py` (the 38 verdict probes of question 4, `v/*.c`); a few hand-written probes (`il/oldpath.c`, `il/oldpathx.cpp`, `il/inv2.c`, `il/inv2x.cpp`, `il/narrow.c`, `il/narrowx.cpp`, written once, never regenerated); `run_il.sh <probe>...` (for each mode: `scripts/cerastes-fe.sh --c23|--c++20 --display_error_number -I include --il_display` -> `il/out/<probe>.<mode>.il`, `--cerastes_walk` -> `.walk`, `ilsum.py` (the P65 tool, a reader of the il_display file) -> `.sum`); `compact.py` (one line per contract attribute of a `.sum`, positions and `<-same` stripped; the printed `{T:}` is `type: lvalue/generated flags`; `{int:}` with no flags is dropped, `P1@0` is `param_ref 1 up=0`, `P1` is `param_ref 1` with `levels_up` 1) and `walkc.py` (one line per attribute of a `.walk`, with the source column `@c` of every node; used for loop clauses, see H7); `run_v.sh` (`build/cerastes verify <probe> --std=c23|c++20 --keep-vpr=v/out/<probe>.<mode>.vpr`), `summarize.sh` (every error category with its line, `v/summary.txt`), `v/results.all.tsv` (name, mode, exit status, seconds, first line; 80 lines, 76 final runs). `pins/` holds the Q3 runs. #### Hazards (read first)

- **H1. `cerastes_old(e)` in C23 folds the macro's `&(e)` when `e` is `*X` (`&*X` -> `X`); in C++20 the `address_of(indirect(...))` stays.** The macro is `#define cerastes_old(e) (*(__typeof__(e)*)cerastes_old_(&(e)))` (`include/cerastes.h:92`). `pp.c:25` `**pp == cerastes_old(**pp) + 1` (`pp_old2`): C23 `old_(cast(indirect(param_ref 1{int **}){int *}))` (`pp.c23.sum`, ATTR L25: `indirect(cast(call(old_, cast(indirect(P1{int **:}){int *:}){const void *:g}){const void *:}){int *:})`), C++20 `old_(cast(address_of(indirect(indirect(P1)){int:L}){int *}))` (`pp.c++20.sum` ATTR L25). The same for `old(*pp)` (`pp.c:29`: C23 `cast(P1{int **})`, C++20 `cast(address_of(indirect(P1){int *:L}))`), `old(***ppp)` (`pp.c:44`), `old(*p->q)` of `struct P` (`chain.c:50`: C23 `cast(points_to_field(P1, field q))`), `old(*gp)` (`gp.c:24`: C23 `cast(var gp)`), `old(*s.q)` (`val.c:26`: C23 `cast(dot_field(P1, field q))`). **No level is lost** (the argument is the address of the place, so the place is `*X`), but the encoder must read the argument `X` of `old_(cast(X))` as: `address_of(Y)` -> the place `Y`; any other `X` -> the place `*X`. Places that are not an `indirect` keep `address_of` in both modes: `old(pp)` (`pp.c:33`: `address_of(P1{int **:L})`), `old(p->q->x)` (`chain.c:29`), `old(sgp->x)` (`gp.c:45`), `old((*pp)->x)` (`ss.c:15`), `old(s.q)` (`val.c:30`: `address_of(dot_field(P1, q){int *:L})`). `old(gp)` of a global pointer is a folded **constant** in C23 (`gp.c:28`: `const[addr abk_variable gp off=0]{const void *}`) and `address_of(var gp)` in C++20 (P63 A5). **`X` is an rvalue tree whose loads (`*pp` in `old(**pp)`) are read in the entry state** (plan item 3), not the post state it is written in. `address_taken` is not set by any of this (see H15).
- **H2. The argument shape of `owns`/`reads` differs by mode, and by whether the place is already `const`.** C (both modes, C spelling): the place node itself, no wrapper (`pp.c23.sum` ATTR L4: `call(cerastes_owns, indirect(indirect(P1@0{int **}){int *}))`), except a narrow pointee (H12). C++ (`cerastes::owns(const T&)`): `reference_to{const T &:g}(lvalue_adjust{const T:Lg}(PLACE))`, e.g. `ppx.c++20.sum` ATTR L4 (`ppx.cpp:4`): `call(rt owns, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(indirect(indirect(P1@0{int **:}){int *:}){int:L}){const int:Lg}){const int &:g})`; when the place's own type is **already const** there is **no `lvalue_adjust`**: `qualx.cpp:7` `owns(*pp)` for `int *const *pp`: `reference_to(indirect(P1@0{int *const *}){int *const:L}){int *const &:g}`. `live` takes the pointer value with an implicit qualification cast in C++ (`cast{const int * implicit}(indirect{int *}(var pp))`, `inv2x.cpp:7`; `ppx.c++20.sum` ATTR L10 `call(rt live, cast(indirect(P1){int *:}){const int *:g})`) and the bare pointer value in C (`pp.c23.sum` ATTR L10 `call(cerastes_live, indirect(P1@0{int **:}){int *:})`).
- **H3. `(*p->q).x` and `p->q->x` are different nodes for the same place; so are `(**pp).x` and `(*pp)->x`.** `chain.c:18` `(*p->q).x > 0`: `dot_field(indirect(points_to_field(P1@0{struct L *}, field q){struct L *}){struct L:L}, field x)` against `chain.c:6` `p->q->x`: `points_to_field(points_to_field(P1@0, field q){struct L *}, field x)`; `ss.c:11` `(**pp).x`: `dot_field(indirect(indirect(P1@0{struct S **}){struct S *}){struct S:L}, field x)` against `ss.c:5` `(*pp)->x`: `points_to_field(indirect(P1@0){struct S *}, field x)`. Identical in C23, C++20 and the `cerastes::` spelling. A place walker must accept both forms at every depth.
- **H4. The `is_lvalue` flag is not a reliable "this is a place" test.** In C a call argument of `cerastes_owns` carries no `L` flag at all (`chain.c23.sum` ATTR L6: `points_to_field(points_to_field(...), field x)` has `{int:}`), while a bare `decreases` argument does (`gp.c:32` `*gp`: `indirect(var gp{int *:}){int:L}`) and the operand of `address_of` does. In C++ the place under `reference_to` has `L`. A loaded pointer in the middle of a path is never `L`: `indirect(indirect(P1){int *:}){int:L}` (`ppx.cpp:4`), the inner `indirect` is the rvalue load. Decide a place by node shape and position (the callee's argument), not by `is_lvalue`.
- **H5. Where a place's own qualifier lives (the `const` rule of 0040 item 2 at the innermost level).** C: the node's `type` is the **unqualified** rvalue type and `orig_lvalue_type` keeps the qualified one: `qual.c:4` `**pp` for `const int **pp`: `qual.c23.il:3085-3087` `type: ... int` / `orig_lvalue_type: ... const int`, `operation.kind: eok_indirect` (`.sum`: `indirect(indirect(P1@0{const int **}){const int *}){int<-const int}`). C++ (`cerastes::reads(**pp)`): the place under `reference_to` is `{const int:L}` directly, with no `lvalue_adjust`; in a value context `{int<-const int}` (`qualx.cpp:4`, ATTR L4 `gt(indirect(indirect(...)){int<-const int}, ...)`). **For a non-const place the `lvalue_adjust` and the `reference_to` carry a `const` that the binding added (`{const int:Lg}`, `{const int &:g}`), compiler-generated**: a check that reads the type of the `lvalue_adjust` or of the `reference_to` would call every place const. Read the node **below** the adjust (the `indirect`/`points_to_field`/`dot_field`/`var`) and take `orig_lvalue_type` if present, else its `type`. See Q2's table.
- **H6. A cell pointer is not visible in the contract/invariant nodes.** `inv.c:13` `cerastes_owns(*q)` with `int *q = &x; int **qq = &q;` (a pointer variable whose address is taken): `indirect{int}(var q{int *})` (`inv.c23.walk`/`walkc`: `inv_cell [invariant on stmk_while @L13] ... call{bool}@55(rt cerastes_owns, indirect{int}@56(var q{int *}@57))`), identical to the invariant of a plain pointer local. Only the variable shows it: `inv.c23.sum` `VAR L10 q : int * storage=sc_auto ... address_taken=TRUE` and `VAR L11 qq : int ** ...` (no flag); same in C++20. The body's write `**qq = i` is `assign(indirect(indirect(var qq){int *}){int:L}, var i)` (`inv.c23.sum`, ROUTINE inv_cell).
- **H7. `il_display` does not display the arguments of a loop's `invariant`/`decreases` attributes**, so the loop-clause chains below are from the walker (`--cerastes_walk`, the tool P59 used), not `il_display`. `inv.c23.il:18830` `attributes:              file-scope attribute@797a146290` on the `stmk_while` (`kind: stmk_while`, `:18833`) and the block `file-scope attribute@797a146290` does not occur anywhere in the dump (`grep -c 'attribute@797a146290$'` = 1, the reference); only the routine-level blocks are printed (`grep -c '^file-scope attribute@' inv.c23.il` = 9, all with `name: "requires"`; the 20 `invariant`/`decreases` attributes of the file have no block). Walker and `il_display` were compared on the routine-level `requires`/`ensures` chains of every probe (types and nesting, by eye on the compacted forms), not node by node.
- **H8. By-value parameters and results in contracts: `s.q` is `dot_field(param_ref{struct PI:L}, field q)`, and the base is the parameter itself.** `val.c23.sum` ATTR L7 (`val.c:7`): `call(cerastes_owns, indirect(dot_field(P1@0{struct PI:L}, field q{int *}){int *}))`; in an `ensures` the parameter is `P1` (levels_up 1, the entry copy: ATTR L26 `dot_field(P1{struct PI:L}, field q)`) and the result binder `r` is `P1@0` (`up=0`): `r.q` is `dot_field(P1@0{struct PI:L}, field q{int *})` (`val.c:38` ATTR L38 `eq(dot_field(P1@0{struct PI:L}, field q{int *}){int *}, P1{int *})`). In a **loop clause** the by-value parameter is a `var`, not a `param_ref`: `inv.c23.walk` `inv_val [invariant ... @L98] ... indirect{int}@56(dot_field{int *}@58(var s{struct PI decl=L94:24 lvalue}@57, field q: int * @ L98:59))`. `r.q->x` (`val.c:42`): `points_to_field(dot_field(P1@0{struct PR:L}, field q){struct R *}, field x)`.
- **H9. A value of a heap-read place in an `ensures` shows no `old`; the C++ `old` of a place is a reference read.** `ppx.c++20.sum` ATTR L25 (`ppx.cpp:25`): `ref_indirect(call(rt old, reference_to(lvalue_adjust(indirect(indirect(P1){int *:}){int:L}){const int:Lg}){const int &:g}){const int &:}){int<-const int:g}`: `eok_ref_indirect` with `type: int`, `orig_lvalue_type: const int`, compiler-generated (`il_def.h:14917`). The plain `**pp` beside it is `indirect(indirect(P1))`, an rvalue read (return state, plan item 3).
- **H10. Positions.** The nodes of the user's operands carry their own source columns (walker `t1.c`: `**pp` at `L3:59`/`L3:60`, `pp` at `L3:61`; `p->q->x` at `L28:58..64` with the first `->` (inner `points_to_field`) at column 59, `q` 61, the second `->` (outer) 62, `x` 64 in `chain.walk` l_old); the nodes the `cerastes_old` macro makes (`eok_indirect`, `eok_cast`, `eok_call`, `eok_address_of`) carry the position of the **macro invocation** (`chain.c23.walk` l_old: `op eok_address_of ... @ L29:5`, `op eok_call ... cerastes_old_ ... @ L29:5`) while the user's operand keeps its own (`@ L29:97`..). In `il_display` every node of an attribute argument has `position.column: 5` (the invocation of `CERASTES_REQUIRES`) and the source column in `position.orig_column` (`qual.c23.il:3103-3105`: `position.column: 5`, `position.orig_column: 60` for the `**pp` of `qual.c:4`); same as P58. A diagnostic about an `old` node must take the position of its operand or of the attribute.
- **H11. The `old`-of-a-path shapes are distinguishable and stay rejected.** `*cerastes_old(*pp) == 1` (`oldpath.c:5`) is `indirect(indirect(cast(call(old_, cast(P1{int **}){const void *:g}))){int **})` in C23 and `indirect(indirect(cast(call(old_, cast(address_of(indirect(P1){int *:L}))...` in C++20 (`oldpath.c23.sum`/`oldpath.c++20.sum` ATTR L5); `cerastes::old(*pp)` as a base: `indirect(ref_indirect(call(rt old, ...)){int *<-int *const:g})` (`oldpathx.c++20.sum` ATTR L5); `old(p)->q->x` (`oldpath.c:9`): `points_to_field(points_to_field(indirect(cast(call(old_, cast(address_of(P1{struct L *:L}))))){struct L *}, field q), field x)`. The `old_` call (C) or `old` call under `ref_indirect` (C++) is the marker; the place itself never contains it.
- **H12. A narrow pointee gets an implicit integer-promotion `cast` around the place in the C spelling (both modes), so a cast hides the outermost level of a heap-read place; it is one level and recoverable.** `narrow.c:5` `cerastes_owns(**pp)` for `char **pp`: `call(cerastes_owns, cast(indirect(indirect(P1@0{char **}){char *}){char:}){int:g})` (`narrow.c23.sum`, `narrow.c++20.sum` ATTR L5); the same for `short` (`:9`), `p->q->c` (`:12`: `cast(points_to_field(points_to_field(P1@0, field q), field c{char}){char:}){int:g}`) and `*p->cq`. The `cerastes::` spelling has no cast for `owns`/`reads` (`narrowx.c++20.sum`: `reference_to(lvalue_adjust(indirect(indirect(P1@0){char *:}){char:L}){const char:Lg}){const char &:g}`) but has one in value reads and around `old` (`narrowx.c++20.sum` ATTR L6: `cast(ref_indirect(call(rt old, ...)){char<-const char:g}){int:g}`). This is P53's wrapper (`char`/`bool`/`short`) extended to heap-read places: nothing new, but the recognizer must peel it at every depth.
- **H13. `cerastes_live`, `owns`, `reads` of a pointer member of a heap-read place are the same recognizer shape as for a parameter.** `chain.c:12` `live(p->q)`: `call(cerastes_live, points_to_field(P1@0{struct L *}, field q{struct L *}){struct L *})`; `chain.c:43` `live(p->q)` for `struct P`: the same with `int *`; `val.c:13` `live(s.q)`: `call(cerastes_live, dot_field(P1@0{struct PI:L}, field q{int *}){int *})`; `gp.c:13` `live(gp)`: `call(cerastes_live, var gp{int *})`; `pp.c:10` `live(*pp)`: `call(cerastes_live, indirect(P1@0{int **}){int *})`. The argument is a pointer **value**, not a place (`live` takes `T *`); it is the load of the (heap-read) pointer place.
- **H14. A global is a bare `enk_variable` in every clause, no `param_ref`:** `gp.c23.sum` ATTR L7 `call(cerastes_owns, var gp{int *})`, ATTR L10 `indirect(var gp{int *})`; `sgp->x` is `points_to_field(var sgp{struct S *}, field x)` (`gp.c:35`). The state in which it is read is the clause's, not the node's (P63 A-facts).
- **H15. `address_taken` of a global is set by the `cerastes::` spelling and not by the C one:** `gpx.c++20.sum` `VAR L4 gp : int * storage=sc_static ... address_taken=TRUE`, `VAR L5 sgp ... address_taken=TRUE`; `gp.c23.sum` and `gp.c++20.sum` (C spelling) have neither (P63's NOTE at the end of A5, repeated). No parameter gets the flag from any contract shape (0 of 14, 14, 14, 17, 18 `VAR`s in `pp.c23`, `pp.c++20`, `ppx.c++20`, `chain.c23`, `val.c++20`). The flag is not a reliable test for a global (every global is a block).
- **H16. The loaded pointer inside a path is a bare rvalue `indirect`, with no cast, in every shape, so no level is hidden except by H12's promotion.** Checked for `pp.c`, `ppp`, `gp.c`, `chain.c`, `ss.c`, `val.c`, `inv.c`: every inner load is `indirect{T *}`/`points_to_field{T *}`/`dot_field{T *}`/`var{T *}` with the pointer type, one node per source `*`, `->` or `.` (see the tables).

Notation as `compact.py`: `P1@0` is the parameter in a `requires` or a loop... "C" is the C spelling in `--c23` **and** `--c++20` unless a column says otherwise (the two modes differ only where marked). "C++" is the `cerastes::` spelling (`*x.cpp`, `--c++20`): every `owns`/`reads` argument is `reference_to(lvalue_adjust(PLACE))` (H2), shown as `ref(PLACE)`, and `old` is `ref_indirect(call(rt old, ref(PLACE)))`, shown as `old(PLACE)`.

The il_display forms of the same expressions inside the loop **body** (`inv.c23.sum`) show the same chains for the reads and writes: `assign(indirect(indirect(var pp{int **}){int *}){int:L}, var i)` (`inv.c:27`), `assign(points_to_field(indirect(var ps{struct S **}){struct S *}, field x){int:L}, var i)` (`inv.c:80`), `assign(indirect(var gp{int *}){int:L}, var i)` (`inv.c:111`), `assign(points_to_field(var q{struct S *}, field x){int:L}, var i)` (`inv.c:48`).

Mode differences found (everything else is identical between `--c23` and `--c++20` for the C spelling): (1) `old(*X)`: the folded `&*` (H1); (2) the bool/int type of `&&`, `<=`, `==` (`{int}` in C23, `{bool}` in C++20) and the routine type of the spec function (`bool (*)(...)` against `bool (*)(...) noexcept`); (3) the tag name (`struct L` against `L`); (4) C++20 `assign` results carry `L` (known, P58). The `cerastes::` spellings differ from the C spelling by H2, H5, H9 and `live`'s cast only.

#### Q2. Qualifiers at each level (`qual.c`, `qualx.cpp`; `qual.c23.sum`, `qual.c++20.sum`, `qualx.c++20.sum`; raw `qual.c23.il:3085-3087`)

`**pp` in a value context and as the argument of `owns`/`reads`; `T` is the node's `type`, `orig` its `orig_lvalue_type` when it differs (`<-`).

| Declaration (`qual.c` line) | `*pp` (C, argument of `owns`/`reads`) | `**pp` (C) | `*pp` (C++ `cerastes::`) | `**pp` (C++ `cerastes::`) | Qualifier of the place the `const` rule of 0040 item 2 must see |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `const int **pp` (`:3`; `q_a` `:4`, `q_f` `:19`) | `indirect{const int *}(P1@0{const int **})`, no `orig` | `indirect{int <- const int}(indirect{const int *}(P1@0))` | `ref(lvalue_adjust(indirect{const int *:L}) -> const int *const:Lg)` (`qualx.cpp:4`) | `ref(indirect{const int:L}(...))`, **no `lvalue_adjust`** (`qualx.cpp:19` for `owns`, `:4` for `reads`) | the innermost place `**pp` is `const int`: `owns(**pp)` rejected, `reads(**pp)` allowed; `*pp` (a `const int *`, itself not const) may be owned |
| `int *const *pp` (`:6`; `q_b` `:7`) | `indirect{int * <- int *const}(P1@0{int *const *})` | `indirect{int}(indirect{int * <- int *const}(P1@0))` | `ref(indirect{int *const:L}(P1@0{int *const *}))`, **no `lvalue_adjust`** (`qualx.cpp:7`) | `ref(lvalue_adjust(indirect{int:L}(indirect{int * <- int *const})) -> const int:Lg)` | `*pp` is `int *const`: `owns(*pp)` rejected; `**pp` is a plain `int` |
| `int **const pp` (`:9`; `q_c` `:10`) | `indirect{int *}(P1@0{int ** <- int **const})` | `indirect{int}(indirect{int *}(P1@0{int ** <- int **const}))` | `ref(lvalue_adjust(indirect{int *:L}) -> int *const:Lg)` | `ref(lvalue_adjust(indirect{int:L}) -> const int:Lg)` | neither `*pp` nor `**pp` is const; the const is on the parameter itself (`P1@0{int ** <- int **const}`) |
| `const int *const *pp` (`:12`; `q_d` `:13`, `q_e` `:16`) | `indirect{const int * <- const int *const}(P1@0{const int *const *})` | `indirect{int <- const int}(indirect{const int * <- const int *const}(P1@0))` | `ref(indirect{const int *const:L})`, no `lvalue_adjust` (`qualx.cpp:13`, `:16`) | `ref(indirect{const int:L}(indirect{const int * <- const int *const}))`, no `lvalue_adjust` | `*pp` const (`owns(*pp)` rejected, `reads(*pp)` allowed), `**pp` const (`owns(**pp)` rejected) |

Raw `il_display` for the C `**pp` of `const int **pp` (`qual.c:4`), `qual.c23.il:3085-3087` and `:3089-3090`:
```
file-scope expr-node@76786a4240
type:                    file-scope type@7678418e00: int
orig_lvalue_type:        file-scope type@76786a3660: const int
...
operation.kind:          eok_indirect
```
and its operand (`qual.c23.il:2960`) `orig_lvalue_type: ... const int **` (the parameter, `param_ref.levels_up: 0`). So: **the place's own qualifier is `orig_lvalue_type` of the C node (when it differs from `type`), or the `type` of the node directly under `reference_to`/`lvalue_adjust` in C++ (H5)**; the `lvalue_adjust` node's `const` is the binding's and must be ignored.

**Findings for the lowering:**
1. At a call, the caller needs the pairwise `lvloc` splits over every callee atom place, loaded ones included, or Silicon's own precondition check reports `insufficient.permission` on a liveness atom although every row passed.
2. Two owned parameters may share a liveness block; a callee keeping one fraction then legitimately fails the other's `>=` row in that case (a fixture-design note).
3. In a loop body a load through `*pp` needs splits against every automatic place, `eb`/`lb` included (0040 item 2's splits after a load).
4. The liveness rows of `eb`/`lb` need the `g ==> lvloc(..) != lvloc(..)` guards against all earlier places (as `loop_reads_alias`).
5. A guarded atom's term in the return sums is `(guard ? a : none)`.
6. The fixtures' loops are hand-simplified (no value snapshots of full places): the emitted automatic value rows of 0038 item 3 must keep `*pp` across a loop that does not write it.
7. Without pass 0 the failure is an ordinary assert, not exit 3: pass 0 fixes the message and the line, not the verdict.
8. Silicon reports only the first failing row of a call; the path stops, so later rows reading through an unheld load are never evaluated.
9. An unframed guard read leaves the method verifying (the chain's dummy): only `f__wf`'s framing assert reports it, with no well-formedness error.

No existing test was touched.

### P71: include mechanics and IL facts for vlibc's `<stdlib.h>` shim (record 0046; macOS and Linux, both modes) **PASS for (a)-(f) on both platforms; no stop condition of the plan (EDG accepts every redeclaration, the shim is reached by every route that matters, the contract's declaration is findable from the IL); one correction of P55, seven findings the encoder must meet and the glibc facts (the `__THROW` exception specification, `__nothrow__` in C, the `#541-D` warning that the system flag hides)**

Evidence in `build/m4.5d1/p71/` (not committed): `p71.sh` (the single runner; it writes its probes and its two IL readers, `ilq.py` and `srcflags.py`, itself), `mac/report.txt` (the run quoted below), `mac/out/` (every `--il_display`, include trace and diagnostic file), `mac/probes/`, `mac/f/` (the Viper), `mac/shims/` (the other copy of vlibc and the throwaway malloc shim), `P71.md` (the same with more excerpts). Tools: the snapshot `build/m4.5d1/p71/bin/cerastes-fe` and `cerastes` (built at `d26a87c`, before any M4.5d1 change); the EDG command line is `verify_main.cpp:305-370` by hand; vlibc `5962865`; macOS 27 SDK, clang 21 scrape. Routes: `sys` (the PLANNED order: `--sys_include=<vlibc>/include/vlibc`, `--sys_include=<vlibc>/include`, the platform's directories, `include/`), `sysi` (`sys` plus a user `-I` of another copy), `incfirst` (the shim as `-I` before the system directories on the command line), `inc` (as `-I` after them, the driver's order for a user `-I`). **The Linux half** (Ubuntu 26.04.1, x86-64, glibc 2.43-2ubuntu2.4, clang 21.1.8 over libc++ 21, EDG scrape version 210108) ran `linux.sh` (the same runner) inside the container `cerastes-m4.5d1-p71` (`ubuntu:26.04` image `cerastes-m4.5d1:runner`, `scripts/ci-linux.sh` then `bootstrap.sh`, cerastes at `7ae05ec`, `cerastes-fe` built clean there) on `matt@clang4.cpp.al`; evidence `build/m4.5d1/p71/linux/report.txt` (a copy of `~/cerastes-m4.5d1/cerastes/build/p71-linux/` on the host, where `out/` holds every listing). Its facts are in "The Linux half" below.

**P55 corrected.** P55 said "only `--sys_include` order does it" because the driver passes the `-I`s after the system directories. EDG keeps `-I` and `--sys_include` in one ordered list (`cmd_line.c:10840-10853`), so the rule is a position before the platform's directories: a leading `-I<vlibc>/include/vlibc` shadows `<stdlib.h>` too (`incfirst`: `<stdlib.h>`, `<cstdlib>`, `<array>`, `<exception>` all open the shim), while `-I` after the system directories does not reach the shim from `<stdlib.h>` in either mode (`inc`). The shim's file record is flagged system by EDG only when a system directory (or a system header that includes it) found it (e). Record 0030 item 3's `--sys_include` is kept for that reason.

**Finding F1 (`#1696` through `-I` under today's order).** `#include <vlibc/stdlib.h>` with `-I<vlibc>/include` (the `inc` route; also `bin/cerastes verify a_explicit.c -I<vlibc>/include`) fails in both modes: `vlibc/stdlib.h, line 17: catastrophic error #1696: cannot open source file "stdlib.h"` at the shim's `#include_next <stdlib.h>`. `#include_next` continues after the directory the file was found in, and the system directories come before `-I`. Under the planned order vlibc's `include/` is itself before the platform's, so `#include_next` continues into them (`sys`, `sysi`: exit 0, no diagnostic).

#### (a) The shim is reached; `<vlibc/stdlib.h>` is the pin

`sys`, `mac/report.txt` section (a) (`--trace_includes`, indentation = include depth):

#### (c) `abort`, `exit`, `_Exit` in the IL (`ilq.py` over `--il_display`; `sys`)

**`decl_position`** (`mac/report.txt` (c); `decls.c:9802-9813` moves it in C++ for a routine with at least one parameter):

| routine | C23 | C++20 |
|---|---|---|
| `abort(void)` | `<SDK>/usr/include/_abort.h:33:7` | `<SDK>/usr/include/_abort.h:33:7` (no parameter: not moved) |

It moves again while it is in a system-flagged file: `c_user_extc_after.cpp` (`#include <stdlib.h>` then a user `extern "C" void exit(int);`) gives `exit` `decl_position = c_user_extc_after.cpp:3:17`, its contract still at vlibc's line; `abort` stays at `_abort.h:33:7`. C23 never moves it: `c_user_after.c` (`void abort(void); void exit(int);` after `<stdlib.h>`) keeps the SDK's position and adds the secondary declarations `c_user_after.c:2:6`, `:3:6`. **The contract's declaration therefore cannot be read from `decl_position`.**

**Attribute entries** (the routine's merged `source_corresp.attributes`, in declaration order; identical in both modes):
- `abort`: `kind=cold family=gnu name=__cold__ @ _abort.h:33:19`; `kind=noreturn family=gnu name=__noreturn__ @ _abort.h:33:26`; `kind=registered family=std namespace_name=cerastes name=ensures syntactic_location=post func @ <vlibc>/include/vlibc/stdlib.h:27:18`.
- `exit`: `noreturn __noreturn__ @ _stdlib.h:165:17`; `ensures @ stdlib.h:30:23`. `_Exit`: `noreturn @ _stdlib.h:215:17`; `ensures @ stdlib.h:33:24`.
- An attribute's `position` is the macro use site (the `CERASTES_ENSURES` on the declaration's line); `orig_seq` is the macro's definition in `cerastes.h`. `does_not_return` is TRUE on the type of all three in both modes, with vlibc present.

**Where the contract's declaration is (the plan's stop condition: findable).** Two ways, both from the IL:
1. Each attribute entry in the routine's list has its own `position`, and its file is the declaring file (`in_verified_file(a->position)` or the library rule). This works in both modes, and for a declaration that was moved or redeclared.
2. Each `a_src_seq_secondary_decl` has its own `attributes`: entry `#1` is the SDK's (`first_declaration=TRUE`, the SDK's attributes only), entry `#2` is vlibc's (`stdlib.h:27:6`, `30:6`, `33:6`; `ensures` only). **Note (`IlEntities::secondary_decls`, `il_query.h:77-84`):** the collector keeps every secondary entry, **including the first declaration** (`first_declaration=TRUE`; its comment, "other than the one `decl_position` names", is not what the IL shows: in C++ exit's entry `#2` is equal to `decl_position`), and `SecondaryDecl` keeps `position` and `declared_type` only, not the declaration's `attributes`. Way 2 needs that field added; way 1 needs nothing.

**Language linkage** (`name_linkage` prints `C` for `nlk_external` and `C++` for `nlk_cplusplus_external`; `parent_scope.kind`):

| declaration | `name_linkage` | type's `routine_name_linkage` (`_is_explicit`) | `parent_scope` | `does_not_return` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `std::exit`/`std::abort`/`std::_Exit` via `<cstdlib>` | `C` | `C` (TRUE) | `sck_file` | TRUE |
| `std::exit(0)` and `::exit(1)` in one program | one routine entity (both calls name the same `routine@...`; `c_std_exit_calls.cpp`) | | | |
| user `extern "C" void abort(void);`, no `<stdlib.h>` | `C` | `C` (TRUE) | `sck_file` | absent (FALSE), no attributes |
| the same after `<stdlib.h>` | `C` (the library entity, three secondary declarations) | `C` | `sck_file` | TRUE, vlibc's `ensures` present |
| user plain `void abort(void);` after `<stdlib.h>` (C++) | `C` (the redeclaration inherits the linkage: one entity) | `C` | `sck_file` | TRUE |
| user plain `void abort(void);`, no header, C++ | `C++` | `C++` (`-`) | `sck_file` | absent |
| user `void abort(void) ensures(true) {}`, no header, C++ | `C++`, `defined=TRUE` | `C++` | `sck_file` | absent; `ensures @ the user's file` |
| `namespace n { void exit(int); }` | `C++` | `C++` | `sck_namespace`, `assoc_namespace n` | absent |
| user plain `void abort(void);`, no header, C23 | `C` | `C` (`-`) | `sck_file` | absent |

So a C++-linkage `abort` can only exist without the library header. **Parameter names do not change:** the routine type's `param-type` of `exit`/`_Exit` has no `name:` field with the shim present, in either mode (the SDK's declaration is unnamed; vlibc's `status` does not enter it; the probe `h_pname.c` shows a later declaration's name does not fill an earlier unnamed parameter), so the Viper formal stays `p_arg__0` (glibc's `__status` stays `p___status__0`, record 0031 item 6).

#### (a) Allocation conversions: the `void *` call is the direct operand of an `eok_cast`, and it is kept

`a_alloc.c` (C23), `a_alloc_both.c` (both modes), `a_alloc.cpp` (C++20); `ilx.py body`. In every shape the call is `enk_operation/eok_call type=void *` whose first operand is `enk_routine malloc` (`type=void *(*)(size_t)`), and its parent is an `enk_operation/eok_cast` to the target pointer type (`il_def.h:13877`, `eok_cast`; the node's `compiler_generated` is the field at `il_def.h:15094`):
